desc: Alexander is an enormous clay pot with a warrior's soul rattling around inside it, walking the Lands Between looking for a fight big enough to prove him. He keeps getting stuck in holes and lava, and every time you dig him out he moves one region closer to the ending he wants, which is a duel with you. He is the friendliest questline in the game and the payoff is one of the best talismans in it, plus the keepsake that finishes Jar-Bairn's story back in Liurnia.
whatItIs: Alexander is an enormous clay pot with a warrior's soul rattling inside, wandering the Lands Between in search of a fight big enough to prove him. Each time he gets stuck in a hole or a lava pool, rescuing him moves him one region closer to the duel he has been building toward.
whyItMatters: The chain pays out the Shard of Alexander talisman, Alexander's Innards, and the thread that finishes Jar-Bairn's story in Liurnia. It breaks if Starscourge Radahn is defeated before the Redmane Castle Plaza meeting, if Crumbling Farum Azula is entered without the Mt. Gelmir stop, or if he is killed at any earlier location.
whenToUse: Begin at the cliffs south-west of Saintsbridge in Stormhill before moving past Limgrave, because the Stormhill and Gael Tunnel rescues are one-time scenes that never replay. Have the Redmane Castle Plaza talk and his summon sign both done before Starscourge Radahn dies, then work through the lava bath south of Fort Laiedd in Mt. Gelmir before stepping into Crumbling Farum Azula, since skipping that last stop means the Dragon Temple Lift duel and its rewards vanish.
name: The path of champions

steps.text: Head to the cliffs south-west of Saintsbridge in Stormhill, where a jar is wedged upside down in a crater and shouting for help. Agree to help, stand behind him and hit him until he pops free, then talk again for an Exalted Flesh.

He shows up next inside Gael Tunnel, blocked by a shutter near the Rear Gael Tunnel Entrance grace. Enter from the Caelid mouth of the tunnel, work back through it to open his door, and exhaust his dialogue.
Trigger the Radahn Festival and he is waiting in the castle plaza listening to the announcement, delighted that a proper war is finally on offer. Speak to him before you drop into the dunes.

lockouts.name: Starscourge Radahn
lockouts.note: kill Radahn without the festival running and this meeting, plus his summon sign for the fight, are gone

steps.text: Summon him for Starscourge Radahn. He is a heavy, tanky phantom who soaks the general's charges well, which makes him one of the better signs on that arena.
After Radahn falls, find him cracked open on the sand near the grace in the Wailing Dunes. Exhaust his dialogue; he plans to refill himself with the bodies of the fallen champions.

He is jammed into another pit on the cliffs above Jarburg, south of the Artist's Shack. Hitting him is not enough this time: throw an Oil Pot over him first, talk, then keep hitting until he slides out. He pays three Exalted Flesh.

Find him bathing in the lava pool south of Fort Laiedd, near a roaming magma wyrm. Ride Torrent onto the sloped rock in front of him and dismount there so the lava cannot reach you, then talk to receive the Jar.

lockouts.name: Crumbling Farum Azula
lockouts.note: skip this meeting and he never appears for the final duel, taking Shard of Alexander and Alexander's Innards with it

steps.text: His summon sign sits just inside the Fire Giant arena. Bringing him along is optional, but he is happy to have watched you kill something that size.
He is standing on a broken platform on the path south-east of the Dragon Temple Lift grace, and he finally asks for the duel he has been building toward. Tell him when you are ready.
Win the duel. He takes it well, asks you to take what is inside him, and leaves the Shard of Alexander and Alexander's Innards on the platform. Exhaust his last lines before you loot.
Carry Alexander's Innards back down to Jarburg and give them to Jar-Bairn, the young jar who calls him uncle.

missables.trigger: defeating Starscourge Radahn
missables.lost: the Redmane Castle Plaza meeting and his summon sign for that fight are both gone.

missables.trigger: entering Crumbling Farum Azula
missables.lost: without the Mt. Gelmir meeting he never spawns at the Dragon Temple Lift, so the duel, Shard of Alexander and Alexander's Innards are all lost.

missables.trigger: killing Alexander at any of the earlier stops
missables.lost: the rest of the chain ends immediately, and Jar-Bairn's Companion Jar goes with it because the innards only drop from the final duel.

missables.trigger: completing step 1 and step 2 (the Stormhill and Gael Tunnel rescues)
missables.lost: each is a one-time scene; miss them and the four Exalted Flesh handed out there are simply never offered.

desc: Boggart is a huge ex-convict in a rusted iron mask who cooks shellfish by the lake and shouts at you until you buy something. He looks like a mugger and behaves like a decent man: he sells back the necklace he took from Rya, hands out an endless supply of the best cheap buff food in the game, and later warns you off the one NPC who is genuinely dangerous. His story only has one ending, and it is a grim one, so the whole point of following it carefully is to take everything he offers before that ending arrives.
whatItIs: Blackguard Big Boggart is a huge ex-convict in a rusted iron mask who cooks shellfish by the Liurnia lakeshore and sells back the necklace he took from Rya the Scout. His questline hands out unlimited cheap buff food and ends grimly, so the goal is to take everything he offers before that ending arrives.
whyItMatters: His shop provides an endless supply of Boiled Prawn and Boiled Crab, and his death drops the Blackguard's Iron Mask, Iron Ball with Ash of War: Braggart's Roar, and the Blackguard's Bell Bearing. The whole line is lost if Volcano Manor is entered before speaking to Rya the Scout, or if the Dung Eater is freed from the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds before every desired item is purchased.
whenToUse: Speak to Rya the Scout in the gazebo at the Boilprawn Shack area first, then walk the shore north-west to meet Boggart and buy at least one Boiled Prawn. After restocking at his Capital Rampart stall, exhaust his dialogue about the Dung Eater before freeing that NPC from his cell.
name: Boggart's questline

steps.text: Ride down to the southern lakeshore and speak to Rya the Scout in the gazebo first. This has to happen before you ever set foot in Volcano Manor, or she moves on and the necklace trade never opens.

lockouts.name: Volcano Manor
lockouts.note: Rya relocates and Boggart's questline can no longer be started

steps.text: Follow the shore north-west from the gazebo to the Boilprawn Shack and talk to the huge man in the iron mask; he has Rya's necklace and is not shy about it.
Choose "Give me the necklace" and then "Deal", and buy Rya's Necklace back from him for a thousand runes rather than trying to take it by force.
Once the necklace is sold, his shop opens properly. Buy at least one Boiled Prawn to advance him; he throws in the "Spread Out" gesture for the custom.

Stock up. Boiled Prawn is unlimited, cheap, and gives a 15 percent physical damage negation buff for a minute, which makes it one of the most useful things you can carry into a boss fight for most of the mid game.
With a prawn bought, his summon sign appears at the Ruin-Strewn Precipice Overlook; call him in against Magma Wyrm Makar and he tanks the dragon happily.
Rest at any grace on the Altus Plateau and he packs up. He reappears in the Capital Outskirts, out on the moat along the northern wall of Leyndell, due west of the Capital Rampart grace.
Buy from his new stall, which now sells an endless supply of Boiled Crab, a straight upgrade on the prawn at the same price. Buy at least one so the recipe stays with his bell bearing later.
Exhaust his talk about the Dung Eater. He was in the same gaol and knows exactly what the man does to corpses, and this is the game quietly warning you what freeing him will cost.
If you go on to free the Dung Eater from his cell under the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, come back and hear Boggart's last line, in which he tells you the killer is close.
Reload the area after that final warning and you find Boggart tied to a chair. Speaking to him triggers the Dung Eater's invasion.

Kill the Dung Eater in that invasion, then return to the chair; Boggart is already dead. Take the Blackguard's Iron Mask, the Iron Ball with Ash of War: Braggart's Roar still fitted, the Blackguard's Bell Bearing and the Seedbed Curse from his body.

Hand the Blackguard's Bell Bearing to the Twin Maiden Husks so the food you were buying is still available, remembering that only the items you actually purchased from him while he lived carry across.

missables.trigger: entering Volcano Manor before speaking to Rya the Scout
missables.lost: Rya leaves the lakeshore, the necklace conversation with Boggart never opens, and his shop and his whole questline become unreachable.

missables.trigger: completing the purchase of a Boiled Prawn before Boggart dies
missables.lost: if you never bought one, the recipe does not transfer to the Blackguard's Bell Bearing and neither the Twin Maiden Husks nor anyone else will sell it.

missables.trigger: completing the purchase of a Boiled Crab before Boggart dies
missables.lost: the same rule applies to the crab, which only exists in his Altus stall.

missables.trigger: completing the release of Dung Eater from the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds
missables.lost: Boggart is murdered and his shop closes for the rest of the run, so buy everything you want first.

desc: Blaidd is Ranni's sworn shadow and the closest thing Elden Ring has to a companion character: he fights beside you at two separate bosses and points you at the next place to go whenever Ranni's plan stalls. His own thread runs alongside hers rather than inside it, which is why it is easy to half-finish. It ends badly no matter what you do, and the gear only drops if you let it run all the way to that ending. Kill him early out of curiosity and you get nothing at all.
whatItIs: Blaidd is Ranni's sworn shadow and a companion-like figure who fights beside you at two separate bosses and points the way forward whenever Ranni's plan stalls. His own thread runs alongside hers and ends badly no matter what, with all the gear dropping only if the story runs to that ending.
whyItMatters: The rewards include the Royal Greatsword, the full Blaidd armour set, the Black Wolf Mask, and a map marker for Nokron. Killing him before Ranni's questline ends drops nothing at all, and the chain restructures if Starscourge Radahn is defeated early or if Ranni's service is never entered.
whenToUse: Trigger the first meeting by performing Finger Snap near the ruined tower in Mistwood, east of Agheel Lake, once Limgrave is open. The chain then threads through the Forlorn Hound Evergaol, Ranni's Rise, the Siofra River Bank, and Redmane Castle, with each step dependent on Ranni's own line having progressed far enough. The final confrontation waits outside Ranni's Rise after Astel, Naturalborn of the Void falls, so keep both threads moving together.
name: Blaidd's questline

steps.text: Ride into Mistwood, east of Agheel Lake, until you hear a long howl coming out of the trees.
Go to Merchant Kale at the Church of Elleh and choose "About the howling in Mistwood". He teaches you the Finger Snap gesture.
Stand near the ruined tower in Mistwood that a Runebear patrols and perform Finger Snap. Blaidd leaps down from the wall. Talk him out and he asks you to find a traitor named Darriwil.
Enter the Forlorn Hound Evergaol in western Limgrave and summon Blaidd for the fight against Bloodhound Knight Darriwil.
Speak to Blaidd outside the evergaol afterwards. He pays you with a Somber Smithing Stone 2 and tells you to name-drop him to the blacksmith in Liurnia.
Enter Ranni's service at the top of Ranni's Rise. A projection of Blaidd appears in the room and tells you he is going down the Mistwood well to look for Nokron.

lockouts.name: Starscourge Radahn
lockouts.note: this meeting is skipped entirely and his story jumps straight to Redmane Castle

steps.text: Ride the Mistwood lift down and find Blaidd near the Siofra River Bank grace. He admits he is stuck and suggests squeezing Seluvis for answers.

lockouts.name: Starscourge Radahn
lockouts.note: this meeting is also skipped

steps.text: Ask Preceptor Seluvis about Nokron at Seluvis's Rise in the Three Sisters, then speak to Sorceress Sellen.
Return to Blaidd and exhaust his dialogue. He works out that Radahn is holding Ranni's fate still, and leaves for the war festival in Caelid.
Once the Radahn Festival opens, Blaidd is standing in the plaza at Redmane Castle. His summon sign sits on the Wailing Dunes battlefield for Starscourge Radahn.
After Radahn dies, speak to Blaidd beside the Starscourge Radahn grace. He marks the crater where the falling star landed, which is the way into Nokron, Eternal City, on your map.

Later, War Counselor Iji seals Blaidd inside the Forlorn Hound Evergaol for fear he will turn on Ranni. Interact with the evergaol to talk to him and choose whether to release him. Either choice leads to the same end.
Visit Iji at his anvil past the Kingsrealm Ruins and pick "Why is Blaidd in the evergaol?" for his side of it.

Take the Dark Moon Ring to Ranni and defeat Astel, Naturalborn of the Void. Blaidd is then waiting outside Ranni's Rise, mad and hostile. Killing him drops the Royal Greatsword along with Blaidd's Armor, Blaidd's Gauntlets and Blaidd's Greaves.
Complete the set from a corpse on the broken walls near Seluvis's Rise, a short ride away, where the Black Wolf Mask lies.
Return to Iji one last time and choose "Blaidd's Death". Reload the area and he too is gone.

rewardNames: (the entrance to Nokron marked on your map)
rewardNotes: the entrance to Nokron marked on your map

missables.trigger: killing Blaidd before Ranni's questline has reached its end
missables.lost: he drops nothing at all, so the Royal Greatsword and his armour pieces are lost for the run.

missables.trigger: defeating Starscourge Radahn early
missables.lost: the Ranni's Rise projection and the Siofra River meeting are both skipped, and Blaidd simply turns up at Redmane Castle instead.

missables.trigger: never entering Ranni's service
missables.lost: Blaidd still appears at the festival as a fellow combatant, but the Nokron thread and the whole second half of his story never open.

desc: Yura wears the garb of the Land of Reeds and spends the game hunting Bloody Fingers, the invaders who prey on other players' worlds. He shows up to bail you out twice before you ever do anything for him, which makes his ending land harder than most. His quest hands over two standout Dexterity weapons and the one crystal tear that makes Mohg's ritual survivable, and every piece of it is gated behind a single hard border: the moment you set foot in the Mountaintops of the Giants, his story is over wherever it happened to be.
whatItIs: Bloody Finger Hunter Yura wears the garb of the Land of Reeds and spends the game hunting the Bloody Finger invaders who prey on other worlds. He bails out the character twice before any favour is given back, and his line hands over two standout Dexterity weapons plus the Purifying Crystal Tear that makes Mohg's ritual survivable.
whyItMatters: The rewards are the Nagakiba, Eleonora's Poleblade, the Purifying Crystal Tear, and a Smithing Stone 5. The entire quest locks the moment Mountaintops of the Giants is entered, so every step must be completed before crossing into that region, and Eleonora's invasion at the Second Church of Marika must be reached for the Poleblade and the Tear.
whenToUse: Find him resting under a ruined arch near the Seaside Ruins grace in Limgrave and exhaust his dialogue to kick off the chain. The next stops fall at Murkwater Coast, the Main Academy Gate, and the Second Church of Marika near the Altus Highway Junction. All of these must be reached before stepping into the Mountaintops of the Giants, since that single border closes the quest wherever it stands.
name: Yura's questline

steps.text: Yura is resting under a ruined arch near the Seaside Ruins grace, south-west of Agheel Lake. Exhaust his dialogue; his summon sign then appears by the lake for the dragon.
Summon him and kill Flying Dragon Agheel, then speak to him again. He tells you what the dragon heart is for and warns you what Dragon Communion costs.

Ride into the ravine north of Agheel Lake, heading for Murkwater Cave. Bloody Finger Nerijus invades; hold out and Yura drops in to fight beside you. This step and the two above can be done in either order.
With Nerijus dead, carry on along the ravine and find Yura sitting under a bridge. Exhaust his dialogue.
A red summon sign sits on the bridge north-east of the academy's main gate. Use it to fight at Yura's side against the Bloody Finger Ravenmount Assassin.

lockouts.name: Mountaintops of the Giants
lockouts.note: Yura is replaced by Shabriri and every remaining step is cancelled

steps.text: Afterwards Yura is standing near where the sign was. Speak to him for a Smithing Stone 5 and a warning about Eleonora, whom he calls the deadliest Bloody Finger alive.

Travel north-west from the Altus Highway Junction grace to the Second Church of Marika. Yura is lying on the ground, mortally wounded, having cut a finger off Eleonora. Speak to him, then take the Nagakiba he leaves behind.

lockouts.name: Mountaintops of the Giants
lockouts.note: the scene never plays and the Nagakiba is left lying wherever he last stood

steps.text: Eleonora, Violet Bloody Finger invades the church a moment later. Kill her for Eleonora's Poleblade and the Purifying Crystal Tear.

However far you got, once you cross into the Mountaintops the quest closes. Shabriri is waiting near the Zamor Ruins grace wearing Yura's body, and the Nagakiba can be picked up off the ground at whichever spot Yura had reached.

missables.trigger: entering Mountaintops of the Giants
missables.lost: the quest locks in place immediately, Shabriri takes Yura's body, and any step you had not reached is gone for the run.

missables.trigger: killing Yura yourself
missables.lost: he drops the Nagakiba on the spot, but the Ravenmount Assassin fight and his final scene are cancelled. Eleonora still invades the Second Church of Marika, so the Poleblade and the Purifying Crystal Tear survive this mistake.

missables.trigger: never reaching the Second Church of Marika before the Mountaintops
missables.lost: Eleonora's Poleblade and the Purifying Crystal Tear are lost, and the tear is the item that makes Mohg's Bloodboon Ritual survivable.

desc: Boc is a demi-human tailor who follows you across the whole game once you rescue him, and he is the only NPC who will resize a helmet or shorten a cape for you at no cost. His quest is a long chain of short conversations rather than a set of fights: free him, win back his mother's needle, then keep finding him at each new region's doorstep. The ending is the part players get wrong, because the kind-sounding option is the one that kills him. Doing it right keeps your free alteration service alive to the credits and hands you the My Lord gesture on the way.
whatItIs: Boc is a demi-human tailor who, once rescued, follows the character across the entire game as a free alteration service for every piece of armour. His quest is a long chain of short conversations spanning five regions, and the ending hinges on a single item found in Hermit Village.
whyItMatters: Done correctly, Boc stays alive to the credits and awards the My Lord gesture along the way. The line breaks if a Larval Tear is given to him or if the "What do you really think?" option is chosen, and killing him at any stage makes the gesture unobtainable and removes the free alteration service entirely.
whenToUse: Free the small tree on the road south-east of Agheel Lake North, then follow him to Coastal Cave for the Sewing Needle and to the Lake-Facing Cliffs for his first service. The critical Prattling Pate "You're Beautiful" must be collected in Hermit Village before reaching the East Capital Rampart stage, or the save becomes impossible.
name: Boc's questline

steps.text: On the road south-east of the Agheel Lake North grace, near Gatefront Ruins, a small tree calls out to you. Hit it or roll into it to break the spell and turn it back into Boc.
Keep talking until he offers to sneak back into the cave his tribe threw him out of, then talk once more so he works up the nerve to go.
Travel to Coastal Cave on the western shore. Boc is lying beaten on the floor right beside the cave's grace, warning you to turn back.
Push through to the end of the cave and kill the Demi-Human Chiefs. They drop the Sewing Needle, his mother's keepsake.
Carry the Sewing Needle back to Boc at the cave entrance and speak to him. He decides to live and to become a seamster like his mother.
Boc is waiting at the Lake-Facing Cliffs grace, the ledge you arrive on when you leave Stormveil. Talk to him and he becomes your personal seamster, altering armour for free from here on.
Open the chest inside the Church of Vows, east of the lake, to take the Gold Sewing Needle.

Hand the Gold Sewing Needle to Boc at the East Raya Lucaria Gate grace. He can now alter demigod garments, which no other service in the game will touch. If you miss him here you can give it to him at any later stop.

Loot Prattling Pate "You're Beautiful" from a body in Hermit Village, the sorcerers' settlement on the south-eastern flank of the mountain. This one item decides how his story ends, so pick it up before you reach the capital.

lockouts.name: step 12
lockouts.note: without the pate in hand Boc cannot be talked out of his rebirth

steps.text: Find Boc beside the Altus Highway Junction grace. If he already has the Gold Sewing Needle he asks permission to call you lord. Agreeing awards the My Lord gesture.
Boc turns up at the East Capital Rampart grace. Once Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon is dead he starts asking about being reborn and requests a Larval Tear.

Use Prattling Pate "You're Beautiful" while standing in front of him. He hears his mother's voice, asks whether you agree, and answering "That's right" settles him for good. He stays at the rampart, still altering your gear, for the rest of the run.
The bad ending, and the one to avoid: hand him a Larval Tear, or refuse and then pick "What do you really think?". Either sends him off to Rennala for a rebirth that kills him.
If you took step 13, he can be found kneeling in human form outside the Raya Lucaria Grand Library, and is dead when the area reloads.

rewardNames: (free armour alterations for the rest of the run)
(alterations to demigod garments after the Gold Sewing Needle)
rewardNotes: free armour alterations for the rest of the run
alterations to demigod garments after the Gold Sewing Needle

missables.trigger: completing step 13 (giving Boc a Larval Tear, or choosing "What do you really think?")
missables.lost: Boc leaves the capital, dies at Raya Lucaria Grand Library, and his free alteration service is gone for the rest of the run.

missables.trigger: killing Boc at any stage
missables.lost: every later step is cancelled, the My Lord gesture is unobtainable, and no other NPC will alter your armour.

missables.trigger: completing step 12 before step 9 is impossible, so a run that skips Hermit Village has no way to save him once he asks for the Larval Tear.

desc: Brother Corhyn is the incantation teacher in Roundtable Hold, and Goldmask is a silent scholar standing on a broken bridge staring at the Erdtree. Their two quests are really one - Corhyn spends the whole game trying to write down what the mute Goldmask is thinking - and it pays out the Mending Rune of Perfect Order, which unlocks the Age of Order ending. It also has one of the strangest puzzles in the game: you have to cast Law of Regression at a statue to work out that Radagon and Marika are the same person, then go tell Goldmask.
whatItIs: Brother Corhyn is the incantation teacher in Roundtable Hold, and Goldmask is a silent scholar kneeling on a broken bridge staring at the Erdtree. Their two quests are really one: Corhyn spends the game trying to write down what the mute Goldmask is thinking, and the pair travel together as far as the Mountaintops of the Giants.
whyItMatters: The line pays out the Mending Rune of Perfect Order, which unlocks the Age of Order ending, plus Goldmask's full armour set and the Radiant Gold Mask. Corhyn's two endings are decided on the bridge south of Stargazer's Ruins before Maliketh, the Black Blade is defeated, and accepting the Frenzied Flame makes the rune unusable unless reversed with Miquella's Needle.
whenToUse: Corhyn appears in the central chamber of Roundtable Hold, and the first field meeting happens north of the Altus Highway Junction once the plateau is open. The pair then move to the Forest-Spanning Greatbridge, the Avenue Balcony in Leyndell, and the bridge south of Stargazer's Ruins in the Mountaintops of the Giants. Cast Law of Regression at the Radagon statue in the Erdtree Sanctuary before the Stargazer's Ruins conversation, and make sure Maliketh, the Black Blade is dead before the final branching scene.
name: Brother Corhyn and Goldmask's questline

steps.text: Find Corhyn in the central chamber of Roundtable Hold. He sells incantations, and his stock grows every time you bring him a prayerbook, so hand over every one you find while you still can.
Once you have reached the Altus Plateau, talk to him again. He announces that he is leaving to go find the scholar Goldmask.
Corhyn is now standing north of the Altus Highway Junction grace, next to the Altus Plateau map marker. Talk to him; he has not found Goldmask.

Go and find Goldmask yourself. He is at the end of the Forest-Spanning Greatbridge, the broken bridge west of the highway, kneeling and facing the Erdtree. Interact with him. While you are there, take the Radiant Gold Mask from the corpse at the north edge of the same broken bridge - it is his mask, but it is not on his body at the end.
Return to Corhyn at the Altus Highway Junction and tell him where Goldmask is.
Go back to the Forest-Spanning Greatbridge, where Corhyn has joined Goldmask, and exhaust his dialogue. From here the two of them travel as a pair.
Both of them turn up near the colosseum in Leyndell. Corhyn is exasperated - Goldmask has stopped moving entirely, stuck on the question of who Radagon was.
Take the lift near the Erdtree Sanctuary up to the Radagon statue and cast Law of Regression in front of it. The truth appears: Radagon is Marika.
Go back and talk to Goldmask to pass on what you saw - he gasps, the only sound he makes in the entire game - and then speak to Corhyn.
The pair move on to the bridge south of Stargazer's Ruins in the Mountaintops. Corhyn is now openly doubting his master's faith.

Decide Corhyn's ending here. Offering him the Tonic of Forgetfulness - the one Tanith gives you during Rya's questline - changes how he finishes, even though he refuses to drink it and it stays in your inventory.

lockouts.name: Maliketh, the Black Blade
lockouts.note: the choice has to be made while they are both still on that bridge

steps.text: Branch A, tonic offered: after Maliketh, the Black Blade is dead and Goldmask has moved on, Corhyn stays on the bridge, still asking the empty air where his master went. Reload and he is gone, leaving his flail, his robe and Corhyn's Bell Bearing.

Branch B, no tonic: after Maliketh, the Black Blade is dead, Corhyn appears in Leyndell, Ashen Capital near the fallen Bolt of Gransax, raving that Goldmask was a madman. Exhaust his dialogue, rest at a grace, and he is gone.

Goldmask's own ending is the same either way. After Maliketh, the Black Blade is dead, his corpse lies on a slope near the colosseum in Leyndell, Ashen Capital. Loot it for the Mending Rune of Perfect Order.
Reload the area and return to the same corpse to pick up Goldmask's Rags, Gold Bracelets and Gold Waistwrap, which complete the set with the mask you already took on the Altus bridge.
After the final boss, use the Mending Rune of Perfect Order when you mend the Elden Ring to take the Age of Order ending.

missables.trigger: before defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade
missables.lost: Corhyn's two endings are decided on the bridge south of Stargazer's Ruins, and offering or withholding the Tonic of Forgetfulness there is the only thing that separates them. He refuses the tonic either way, but the act of offering it still counts.

missables.trigger: before entering the Frenzied Flame Proscription
missables.lost: accepting the Frenzied Flame forces the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending, which makes the Mending Rune of Perfect Order unusable unless you reverse it with Miquella's Needle.

missables.trigger: Attacking Goldmask makes him vanish, dropping no runes and no items, and he only comes back after you rest at a Site of Grace.

desc: Ymir is the courteous high priest of a lakeside cathedral in eastern Scadu Altus, and he wants three ancient bells rung on his behalf. Doing so walks you through two hidden finger ruins for a pair of upgraded seed talismans, then opens a hatch beneath his own throne that leads to Metyr, Mother of Fingers - one of the DLC's remembrance bosses. The line ends badly for everyone but you: Ymir tries to become a mother himself, his bodyguard Jolán turns on you, and their deaths pay out a sorcery staff, a full armour set, a rare glintstone spell and one of two night weapons. It is also the calmest questline in the expansion to follow, because almost every step happens in the same room.
whatItIs: Count Ymir is the courteous high priest of a lakeside cathedral in eastern Scadu Altus, and he wants three ancient bells rung on his behalf. The quest walks through two hidden finger ruins, opens a hatch beneath his throne leading to Metyr, Mother of Fingers, and ends with both he and his bodyguard Jolan dead.
whyItMatters: The rewards include Crimson Seed Talisman +1, Cerulean Seed Talisman +1, the Maternal Staff, the full High Priest armour set, and either the Swordhand of Night Jolan spirit ash or the Sword of Night depending on which iris is given. Only one of the two final rewards can be taken in a single playthrough, and Jolan's summon signs vanish once she turns hostile after the throne interaction.
whenToUse: This needs the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Ride east along the Church District Highroad to the Cathedral of Manus Metyr in Scadu Altus, speak to both Count Ymir and Jolan there, then ring the bells at the Finger Ruins of Rhia and Fingerstone Hill before returning to the throne for the final confrontations.
name: Count Ymir and Jolán's questline

steps.text: Ride east along the Church District Highroad and drop down the side track to the flooded cathedral guarded by marionette soldiers and horned turtles; the grace sits in the front hall.
Speak to Count Ymir on the throne beyond that hall and empty every line, including the "Ask about glintstone sorcery" topic. He hands over a hollowed stone necklace and the first ruins map.
Turn back into the hall and talk to Jolán, the black-armoured swordhand leaning on a pillar. She is icy but harmless, and speaking to her now unlocks her warmer dialogue later.
Follow the pale southern shoreline east until a beached stone-coffin ship lets you climb to a ledge overlooking a ring of buried stone hands.
Walk in to the hanging bell at the centre and ring it. The Crimson Seed Talisman +1 is left behind where it swung.
Report back to Ymir. He gives the second ruins map, and two Finger sorceries appear in his stock.
Speak to Jolán again. Having earned her count's trust, she introduces herself properly and offers the Night to you.
(Optional) Look for Jolán's summon sign before the Messmer the Impaler fog gate and call her in.

lockouts.name: step 17
lockouts.note: Jolán turns hostile and every summon sign of hers disappears

steps.text: (Optional) Look for her second sign in the Hinterland, where two mounted sentinels guard the bridge road north.

lockouts.name: step 17
lockouts.note: Jolán turns hostile and every summon sign of hers disappears

steps.text: Take the road running south-east from the Hinterland Bridge into Scaduview and ring the second bell for the Cerulean Seed Talisman +1.
Return to Ymir a third time. He gives the Beloved Stardust talisman and a last map, which points at the ground under his own cathedral.
Empty Jolán's new dialogue, then rest at the grace or quit to the title screen so the area reloads and Ymir leaves his seat.
Interact with the now-empty throne. It slides aside and reveals a ladder into the ruin buried beneath the cathedral floor.
Cross the buried ruin. Swordhand of Night Anna, Jolán's puppeted sister, invades on the approach to the bell; killing her drops the Claws of Night.
(Optional) Climb back up and pick the dialogue option telling Jolán that a swordhand of night attacked you underground. She refuses to hear it, but the exchange is unique.
Ring the third bell at the heart of the ruin. It carries you elsewhere, into an arena of drifting stars, where Metyr, Mother of Fingers waits and drops the Remembrance of the Mother of Fingers.
Go back up and touch Ymir's throne once more. Jolán invades first and fights alone; put her down.

Count Ymir, Mother of Fingers rises immediately afterwards, weaving finger sorceries and calling fingercreepers to him. His death yields the Maternal Staff, all four High Priest pieces and Ymir's Bell Bearing.
Leave by the western door into the little cemetery and take Cherishing Fingers from the grave Ymir was kneeling beside.
Reload the area one final time and find Jolán, alive and grieving. Give her an Iris of Grace for the Swordhand of Night Jolán ashes, or an Iris of Occultation for the Sword of Night katana.

lockouts.name: step 20
lockouts.note: only one of the two rewards can ever be taken in a single playthrough

steps.text: (Optional) Carry the Swordhand of Night Jolán ashes to the puppet of Anna standing at the top of the tower west of the cathedral and interact with it to fuse the sisters into Jolán and Anna; interacting again splits them back apart.

rewardNames: Remembrance of the Mother of Fingers (remembrance)

missables.trigger: completing step 17
missables.lost: Jolán turns hostile and every summon sign of hers disappears.

missables.trigger: completing step 20
missables.lost: only one of the two rewards can ever be taken in a single playthrough.

desc: D is a fundamentalist knight in gold-trimmed plate who hunts Those Who Live in Death, and he is your way into the Deathroot trade with Gurranq at the Bestial Sanctum. He also has a twin brother who shares his soul, which is why this questline does not end when he does. Fia murders him, and if you carry his armour down to the brother waiting in Nokron, the story finishes with a revenge you only get to watch. It is the counterweight to Fia's line: running one all the way means watching the other one lose.
whatItIs: D, Hunter of the Dead is a fundamentalist knight in gold-trimmed plate who hunts Those Who Live in Death, and he is the gateway to the Deathroot trade with Gurranq at the Bestial Sanctum. He has a twin brother who shares his soul, so the questline does not end when he does; Fia murders him and the story finishes with a revenge scene in Deeproot Depths.
whyItMatters: The rewards are the Litany of Proper Death incantation, Order's Blade, the Twinned Armor, and the Inseparable Sword. The chain breaks if Fia kills D before the Weathered Dagger is handed over, if the brother is killed in Nokron before the ending scene, or if Deeproot Depths is entered before Fia's line resolves.
whenToUse: Meet him on the road near Saintsbridge in northern Limgrave and let him introduce the Deathroot trade at the Bestial Sanctum on Greyoll's Dragonbarrow. From there his appearances rotate through Roundtable Hold, the Black Knife Catacombs, and the Aqueduct-Facing Cliffs where his twin waits. The closing scene sits at the Prince of Death's Throne in Deeproot Depths, and it unlocks only after Fia's own questline has run to its end.
name: The twins who hunt the dead
questName: The twins who hunt the dead

steps.text: He is standing on the road near Saintsbridge in northern Limgrave, warning travellers away from the ruined village to the east. Hear him out.
Clear Summonwater Village and kill the Tibia Mariner (Limgrave) holding it for your first Deathroot. He walks into the village afterwards and offers to introduce you to the beast who eats the stuff.
Take him up on it and make the trip to the Bestial Sanctum out on Greyoll's Dragonbarrow, where Gurranq will swap beast incantations for every Deathroot you bring him.
He turns up in the hub whether or not you ever met him in the field, sitting by the lobby table. With a Deathroot on you he makes the same offer here.
Once you have spoken to Gurranq he opens a small stock of Golden Order incantations, Litany of Proper Death and Order's Blade, and calls you brother-in-arms.

His summon sign now appears at two fights he cares about: the Tibia Mariner (Liurnia of the Lakes) out on the lake, and the Black Knife Assassin (Bellum Highway) sealed inside the Black Knife Catacombs.
Push Fia's questline until she gives you the Weathered Dagger and asks you to find its owner. Show it to D; he recognises it as his own and takes it.
Reload the hub. The room at the end of the eastern wing is unlocked, D is dead on the floor, and Fia is standing over him. Take the Twinned Armor and the rest of his plate.

Carry the armour to the ruined city under Limgrave. His twin, D, Beholder of Death, is slumped outside the Valiant Gargoyles' arena past the Hallowhorn Grounds, barely able to form words. Give him the set.

lockouts.name: step 12
lockouts.note: hand him a set you took by killing D yourself and he turns hostile on the next reload, dropping his sword and the armour and ending the story on the spot

steps.text: (Optional) Reload and his summon sign appears for Valiant Gargoyle & Valiant Gargoyle (Twinblade), the duo blocking the coffin ride down to the roots.
Finish Fia's questline. Once the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince is in your hands, the brother is standing over her corpse at the foot of Godwyn, jeering at the Prince of Death.
Reload one last time. He is gone, satisfied, and the Inseparable Sword and Twinned Armor are lying where he stood.

missables.trigger: completing step 8 (letting Fia kill D)
missables.lost: kill D yourself for his armour instead and his brother turns on you the moment you hand it over, so the Nokron summon sign and the quiet ending in Deeproot Depths are both lost.

missables.trigger: completing step 7 (handing over the Weathered Dagger)
missables.lost: Fia has to reach that point in her own line first, and if D is dead before she offers the dagger neither story can finish.

missables.trigger: entering Deeproot Depths
missables.lost: the brother only moves there after Fia's line resolves, so a run that never finishes Fia's questline leaves the Inseparable Sword where he cannot drop it.

missables.trigger: killing D, Beholder of Death in Nokron
missables.lost: you get the sword and armour straight away, but the ending scene at the Prince of Death's Throne never happens.

desc: Dane belongs to the Dryleaf Sect, ascetics who read the falling leaves of the Erdtree as a sign that it was time to look for a new god, and he has served Miquella longer than Leda has. He does not speak; not to you, and by Leda's own account not to her either in all the years they have known each other. His whole quest is a letter, a gesture and a fistfight, which makes it the shortest in the expansion and the only way to get an unarmed martial-arts weapon before the very end of the story.
whatItIs: Dryleaf Dane belongs to the Dryleaf Sect, ascetics who read the falling leaves of the Erdtree as a sign to look for a new god, and he has served Miquella for a very long time. He does not speak to anyone, so the entire quest is a gesture, a fistfight, and a few pieces of armour scattered across the Land of Shadow.
whyItMatters: Winning the bout at Moorth Ruins drops the Dryleaf Arts and Dane's Hat, while the remaining outfit pieces sit on a corpse north of the Recluses' River Downstream or on his body in the Cleansing Chamber Anteroom. The duel and the hat are both lost if the Sealing Tree at Church of the Bud is burned before the fight happens, and his cooperator sign for Romina, Saint of the Bud is gone the same way.
whenToUse: This line requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Reach Scadu Altus by defeating Rellana, Twin Moon Knight in Castle Ensis or by unsealing the spiritspring behind the Fort of Reprimand, then read the Monk's Missive at the Highroad Cross. Perform the challenge gesture it describes at Moorth Ruins and win the bout before the Sealing Tree at the Church of the Bud is set alight, because once that tree burns Dane leaves for good and the Dryleaf Arts are lost.
name: Dryleaf Dane's questline

steps.text: Get into Scadu Altus, either by beating Rellana, Twin Moon Knight in Castle Ensis or by riding the spiritspring that has to be unsealed behind the Fort of Reprimand, and make your way to the Highroad Cross grace.
On the broken wall right beside that grace lie the May the Best Win gesture and the Monk's Missive, a letter from a monk telling you to seek him east and to challenge him without words. Take both.
Ride east from the cross to Moorth Ruins. Dane is standing at the grace there in a robe and arm wraps, and he will not respond to anything you say.
Open the gestures menu, set May the Best Win, and perform it all the way through while facing him. He seals the ruins off and duels you one on one, kicking and casting Discus of Light.
Win the bout. The arena opens again and Dane leaves the Dryleaf Arts and Dane's Hat on the ground next to the Moorth Ruins grace.

lockouts.name: the burning of the Sealing Tree at Church of the Bud
lockouts.note: Dane abandons Moorth Ruins and the duel can never be fought

steps.text: Optional: his gold sign sits outside the arena of Romina, Saint of the Bud, and it is there whether or not you beat him at the ruins. Summoning him changes nothing about his quest.

lockouts.name: Romina, Saint of the Bud
lockouts.note: his cooperator sign for that fight

steps.text: The rest of his outfit is not on him. Work through the Shadow Keep and solve the Domain of Dragons painting, then take the corpse under the waterfall north of the Recluses' River Downstream grace for the Dryleaf Robe, the Dryleaf Arm Wraps and the Dryleaf Cuissardes.

Whatever you did to him at Moorth Ruins, Dane is one of the enemies waiting with Leda in the Cleansing Chamber Anteroom. Put the whole band down and his body carries Dane's Footwork, his own kick-based style, which he learned standing under a waterfall. Killing him is also the only time he speaks: a last plea for Miquella to rise.

missables.trigger: before completing the burning of the Sealing Tree at Church of the Bud
missables.lost: Dane leaves Moorth Ruins for good, and with him the duel, the Dryleaf Arts and Dane's Hat.

missables.trigger: before defeating Romina, Saint of the Bud
missables.lost: his cooperator sign for that fight.

desc: The Dung Eater is a serial killer in omen armour who defiles corpses so their souls can never return to the Erdtree. His spirit haunts a corner of the Roundtable while his body rots in a cell under Leyndell, and he will only deal with you once you are carrying proof of his work. Follow him and you unlock one of the game's endings, the Blessing of Despair, plus his curved greatsword and his armour. It is a long errand: you must find five Seedbed Curses scattered across three late areas, free him, beat him in an invasion, and then feed them to him one at a time.
whatItIs: The Dung Eater is a serial killer in omen armour who defiles corpses so their souls can never return to the Erdtree, and his spirit haunts a corner of Roundtable Hold while his body rots in a cell under Leyndell. His questline is a long errand: find five Seedbed Curses across three late areas, free him, beat him in an invasion, and feed the curses to him one at a time.
whyItMatters: The chain unlocks the Blessing of Despair ending and drops the Sword of Milos and the full Omen Set. It breaks if Blackguard Big Boggart is killed or ignored before the Seedbed Curse he carries is collected, if Seluvis's Potion is administered in the cell, or if he is killed before the invasion step.
whenToUse: Touch any grace on the Altus Plateau to make his apparition appear in the western corner of Roundtable Hold. The first Seedbed Curse hides in the East Capital Rampart area, and finding it is what unlocks the Sewer-Gaol Key and the location of his real body under the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds. Once he is free, the remaining curses scatter across the West Capital Rampart, the Audience Pathway in Volcano Manor, and the Prayer Room in Elphael, Miquella's Haligtree.
name: The seedbed curse

steps.text: Touch any grace on the plateau. That single flag is what makes his apparition appear back at the hub, sitting in the western end past Gideon's study.
Speak to the apparition. He has no interest in you until he can smell his own handiwork on you, so leave and go find a curse first.

From the East Capital Rampart grace push into the city, take the first lift down, and climb the ladder in the perfumer's room to the top floor of the cracked-roof building. A Seedbed Curse sits on the seated corpse there.
Return with the curse in your pouch and exhaust him. He now hands over the Sewer-Gaol Key and tells you exactly where his real body is chained.

From the Underground Roadside grace in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, drop through the open grate to the left as you leave the room and follow the passage past the miranda flowers. Fingercreepers guard the door. Unlock the cell and choose to let him out.
(Optional) With him loose, his summon sign is available for Mohg, the Omen down in the Forsaken Depths and, alongside Melina, for Morgott, the Omen King.
He leaves the Roundtable with a note daring you to meet him at the moat. Go to the water below the capital's outer ramparts, where Blackguard Big Boggart has set up, and talk to Boggart about him.

Reload the area. Boggart is dying; hear him out and take the Seedbed Curse, Blackguard's Bell Bearing, Iron Ball and Blackguard's Iron Mask from his body. The Dung Eater invades moments later and drops the Sword of Milos when beaten.

lockouts.name: step 7
lockouts.note: kill Boggart yourself before that conversation and the curse he carries, along with his bell bearing and mask, cannot be recovered

steps.text: He is back in his corner, and now he wants what he asked for: you are to defile his own flesh with the curses, over and over.
Collect the second capital curse: it lies inside the Fortified Manor room on the West Capital Rampart side, the room that mirrors where his apparition stands in the hub.
Take the Volcano Manor curse from the ground floor of the hall directly opposite the sending gate by the Audience Pathway grace.
The last two are in Elphael: one on the western balcony overlooking the ballista courtyard with the putrid avatar, and one in the dark room straight below the chamber holding two cleanrot knights.
With five in hand, go back down to his cell and choose to use them. Feed all five, then take the Mending Rune of the Fell Curse from his corpse and reload to loot the Omen Set.

(Alternative ending) If you would rather end him, administer Seluvis's Potion in the cell instead. He becomes a mindless thrall, you can kill him safely for his gear, and Preceptor Seluvis's own questline stays intact.

rewardNames: Mending Rune of the Fell Curse (key item)

missables.trigger: completing step 7 (asking Boggart about the Dung Eater)
missables.lost: kill or ignore Blackguard Big Boggart instead and the curse he drops, along with Blackguard's Bell Bearing, Iron Ball and Blackguard's Iron Mask, cannot be obtained. He also has to have been met earlier at the Boilprawn Shack in Liurnia of the Lakes for him to be sitting at the moat at all.

missables.trigger: completing step 14 (administering Seluvis's Potion)
missables.lost: the potion turns him into a puppet on the spot and the Mending Rune of the Fell Curse is gone for this playthrough.

missables.trigger: killing him in his cell before step 8
missables.lost: the invasion never happens, so Sword of Milos and the mending rune are both lost.

missables.trigger: entering Miquella's Haligtree
missables.lost: two of the six obtainable curses only exist in Elphael, so a run that skips the Haligtree needs every other curse, including Boggart's, to reach five.

desc: Ensha is the silent, bone-plated figure propped against the wall outside Gideon's study, and for most of the game he does nothing at all. He is a timed ambush rather than a conversation: the moment you carry half of the Haligtree Secret Medallion into Roundtable Hold he invades the hub itself, which is the only invasion that ever happens there. Kill him and you walk away with an Dexterity and Arcane fist weapon, a full armour set, and the follow-up conversation with Gideon that points at the medallion's other half.
whatItIs: Ensha is the silent, bone-plated figure propped against the wall outside Gideon's study in Roundtable Hold, and for most of the game he does nothing at all. He is a timed ambush: the moment half of the Haligtree Secret Medallion is carried into the Hold, he invades the hub itself.
whyItMatters: Killing him drops the Clinging Bone fist weapon, the full Royal Remains armour set, and the "What Do You Want?" gesture. The gesture can only be taken while he is still alive outside the study, so talk to him before carrying a medallion half into Roundtable Hold, and the Gideon follow-ups about the secret medallions are lost if Maliketh, the Black Blade is defeated first.
whenToUse: Talk to him in Roundtable Hold early, before any late-game errands. The actual fight triggers when either medallion half is picked up at the Village of the Albinaurics or the Castle Sol Rooftop, so the confrontation lands in the late game regardless of when the conversation started.
name: Ensha's ambush

steps.text: Accept Melina's invitation and fast travel to the Hold, then take the corridor ahead and to the left from the arrival point.
Find Ensha leaning on the wall outside Gideon's study and talk to him; he never says a word, but the attempt teaches you the "What Do You Want?" gesture.

lockouts.name: Ensha's invasion of Roundtable Hold
lockouts.note: the gesture is gone once he is dead

steps.text: Leave him alone for now. Nothing else about him changes until you are hunting the route into Miquella's Haligtree, so treat the rest of this as a late-game errand.

Take one of the two medallion halves. The right half belongs to Old Albus, who is hiding as a pot on the slope above the village grace, so roll into the pot or hit it to break the illusion and then exhaust his dialogue.
The other option is the left half, sitting on the tower roof past Commander Niall at Castle Sol; either half on its own is enough to set the trap off.
Fast travel back to the Hold with a medallion half in your inventory. Ensha drops on you as an invader in the northern corridor before you get anywhere near Gideon.

Fight him. He is frail for this point in the game, opens with a Meteorite Staff casting Collapsing Stars to shove you around, and does his real damage with the Clinging Bone in melee, so close the gap and stay on him.
Loot the Clinging Bone from his body, then walk to the spot where he used to stand; his Royal Remains armour is lying there waiting to be picked up.
Go into the study and ask Gideon "About Ensha"; he shrugs the ambush off as his man overreaching and offers an apology.

lockouts.name: Maliketh, the Black Blade
lockouts.note: Gideon becomes hostile and the conversation is lost

steps.text: Follow that with "About the secret medallions" so he tells you where the half you are still missing is kept, which is the fastest legitimate pointer to the Consecrated Snowfield route.

lockouts.name: Maliketh, the Black Blade
lockouts.note: the hint is lost with him

missables.trigger: completing Ensha's invasion of Roundtable Hold
missables.lost: the "What Do You Want?" gesture can only be taken from him while he is still alive and standing outside the study, so talk to him before you ever carry a medallion half into the Hold.

missables.trigger: defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade
missables.lost: Gideon turns hostile in the Ashen Capital, so the "About Ensha" and "About the secret medallions" follow-ups are gone.

desc: Fia sits in a side room of the Roundtable offering to hold Tarnished, and every embrace costs you five percent of your maximum health while the charm she gives you is in your bag. She is not the harmless comfort she looks like: she serves Godwyn, the Prince of Death, and she is working toward a rune that would write deathlessness into the Golden Order itself. Her line runs through three other people's stories and ends with a dragon fight in a dream, and its prize is one of the three mending runes you can carry to the final boss.
whatItIs: Fia sits in a side room of Roundtable Hold offering to hold the Tarnished, and every embrace costs a share of maximum health while the charm she gives is in the bag. She serves Godwyn, the Prince of Death, and her line runs through three other people's stories before ending with a dragon fight in a dream.
whyItMatters: The prize is the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince, one of the mending runes carried to the final boss, plus Baldachin's Blessing and Radiant Baldachin's Blessing. The chain breaks if D, Hunter of the Dead is killed before the Weathered Dagger is given to him, if Ranni's line is never completed, or if Fia is killed at any point.
whenToUse: Find her in the bedroom off the eastern wing of Roundtable Hold and accept the embrace to start the chain. Her line then threads through the Black Knife Catacombs on the Bellum Highway, the Redmane Castle Plaza, and the Divine Tower of Liurnia, each step dependent on D's line and Ranni's line having progressed far enough to support it. The final fight with Lichdragon Fortissax and the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince both resolve at the Prince of Death's Throne.
name: The Deathbed Companion

steps.text: Find her lying in her bedroom off the hub's eastern wing, the one with the mirror by the door. Accept her embrace and she gives you Baldachin's Blessing; be aware her keepsake shaves five percent off your maximum HP while you hold it.
Once Rogier has moved into the hub and started talking about the Night of Black Knives, ask her about knifeprints. She hands over the Knifeprint Clue.
Clear the Black Knife Catacombs on the Bellum Highway and beat the Black Knife Assassin (Bellum Highway) waiting past the tomb's first boss for the Black Knifeprint, then take that to Rogier.
Trigger the Radahn Festival at Redmane Castle. That flag is what makes Fia produce the Weathered Dagger and ask you to return it to its owner.
Put the Weathered Dagger in the hands of D, Hunter of the Dead, who recognises it and offers to carry it home himself. Then reload the hub.

lockouts.name: step 6
lockouts.note: kill D yourself instead and the dagger has nobody to go to, which stops Fia where she stands

steps.text: The sealed room at the far end of the eastern wing is finally open, and she is standing over D's body. Exhaust her and she leaves the hub for good.

Fight down to Fia's Champions, a staged gauntlet that opens with one phantom, answers it with a spectre of Rogier, and finishes with two more champions and Lionel the Lionhearted. Rest at the grace beyond once they are down. She is waiting at the foot of Godwyn's ruined body.

She offers to let you end her. Answer that you want to be held instead; picking the other line does not close anything and you can change your mind by speaking again. While held, choose to talk in secret and she explains the cursemark.

Reach the Divine Tower of Liurnia, which needs the Carian Inverted Statue that Ranni the Witch pays for the Fingerslayer Blade. Set the statue on the pedestal inside the Carian Study Hall to flip the building, then climb through it.
On the tower's roof, take the Cursemark of Death from the discarded body Ranni left behind, alongside the Stargazer Heirloom.
Return, talk in secret again until the option to hand over the Cursemark of Death appears, and give it to her. She pays you the Radiant Baldachin's Blessing.
Exhaust her dialogue, then rest and reload to find her asleep against the Prince of Death.
Touch her body to fall into the Deathbed Dream and fight Lichdragon Fortissax, a red lightning duel fought in a sealed dream with no grace of its own. Winning drops you back beside her body.
Take the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince from her body. Reload once more and she is dead in a different sense: D, Beholder of Death is standing over her, having come for his brother's sake.

rewardNames: Mending Rune of the Death-Prince (key item)

missables.trigger: completing step 5 (giving D, Hunter of the Dead the Weathered Dagger)
missables.lost: kill D yourself and there is nobody to receive the dagger, so Fia never moves to Deeproot Depths and the mending rune is lost.

missables.trigger: completing step 2 (asking Fia about knifeprints)
missables.lost: Rogier has to reach the Roundtable and open the subject first, so a run that never touches his questline cannot start hers.

missables.trigger: completing step 9 (trading the Fingerslayer Blade to Ranni for the Carian Inverted Statue)
missables.lost: without Ranni's line there is no way up the Divine Tower of Liurnia and no Cursemark of Death.

missables.trigger: killing Fia at any point
missables.lost: the mending rune, the Radiant Baldachin's Blessing and the Lichdragon Fortissax fight all vanish with her.

desc: Queelign is one of Messmer's fire knights, and he introduces himself by kicking your door in twice. Beat both of his invasions and the second one leaves an iron key; that key opens a locked prayer room deep in the Shadow Keep, where you find the same knight out of armour, curled on the floor begging Marika for a scrap of grace she is never going to send. What you do with him is a one-line decision made with an eyeball: hand him an Iris of Grace and he dies believing he was answered, leaving his spirit ash behind, or hand him an Iris of Occultation and he dies believing he was rejected, leaving his greatsword. You cannot have both in one run, and the questline survives the expansion's point of no return, so there is no rush.
whatItIs: Fire Knight Queelign is one of Messmer's fire knights, and he introduces himself by kicking a door in twice in the Gravesite Plain and the Church of the Crusade. Beat both invasions and the second drops a Prayer Room Key that opens a locked room deep in the Shadow Keep, where the same knight sits out of armour begging Marika for a scrap of grace.
whyItMatters: Winning both invasions drops the Crusade Insignia and the Ash of War: Flame Skewer, and the second kill leaves a key that opens a locked prayer room in the Shadow Keep. Inside, a single iris handed to the kneeling knight decides whether the Fire Knight Queelign spirit ash or Queelign's Greatsword is the final reward, and the other is lost for that playthrough.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is required to find him. Clear the two invasion sites at the Small Private Altar and the Church of the Crusade in the Gravesite Plain, then collect either an Iris of Grace from the Storehouse or an Iris of Occultation from the Fort of Reprimand. Unlock the prayer room at the Church District Entrance with the key from the second kill and make the iris choice there.
name: Fire Knight Queelign's questline

steps.text: Work up through Belurat until you reach the graveyard plaza a short way north of the small altar grace. Queelign invades here in full fire-knight plate.
His other ambush waits at the blackened church on the western plateau, under the beheaded statue of Marika.
Whichever of the two you clear first drops the Crusade Insignia talisman.
The second time you put him down he drops the Ash of War: Flame Skewer and the prayer room key. Both invasions must be won; the key never appears from a single one.
Collect an iris before you go looking for him. An Iris of Grace sits below the first floor of the storehouse: take the lift on the left down to the chamber packed with jar innards.
(Alternative) A second Iris of Grace lies in the church on the climb toward the Scadutree Avatar, behind the tree-worship sanctum.
For the darker choice, an Iris of Occultation is hidden in the gore-strewn fort on the south-eastern plateau: go in, turn left, and drop through the hole in the floor into an ambush.
(Alternative) A second Iris of Occultation drops from the northern of the two ulcerated tree spirits in the lower church district, reachable once the keep's water has been drained.
Take the key to the house of worship in the church district and unlock the prayer room door. Queelign is inside, unarmoured and praying.

Exhaust his prayer, then give him one iris. Grace convinces him he has been forgiven and he leaves behind the Fire Knight Queelign spirit ash; occultation convinces him he has been cast out and he leaves Queelign's Greatsword.

lockouts.name: step 10
lockouts.note: the reward tied to the other iris is gone for that playthrough

missables.trigger: completing step 10
missables.lost: the reward tied to the other iris is gone for that playthrough.

desc: Gostoc is the hunched gatekeeper who greets you at the doors of Stormveil Castle, and he is quietly robbing you the whole time you are inside it. Once he starts shadowing you through the castle he skims a share of every rune pile you drop on death, and the only way to stop him is to hunt him down in his hiding spots and confront him. Do that and he turns into a useful in-dungeon merchant instead. His story then folds into Nepheli Loux's: leave him alive and he ends up standing behind her throne, selling the best upgrade stone in the game.
whatItIs: Gatekeeper Gostoc is the hunched gatekeeper at the doors of Stormveil Castle, and he is quietly skimming a share of every rune pile dropped on death while inside. Once confronted in his hiding spots he turns into a useful in-dungeon merchant, and his story folds into Nepheli Loux's questline.
whyItMatters: Left alive and un-hostile, he ends up behind Nepheli's throne selling an Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone, and he also drops the Grace Mimic talisman. Killing him removes the Grace Mimic, his shop, the smithing stone, and blocks Nepheli Loux's questline; making him hostile without killing him requires an Absolution from the Church of Vows to repair.
whenToUse: Enter Stormveil Castle through the front gate in Limgrave and pick the main entrance dialogue to set the whole chain in motion. Work through each of his hiding spots at the Stormveil Cliffside ledge, the western wall ground floor, the Rampart Tower roof, and the lift-tower platform, then confront him at the gatehouse. Keep him alive through Godrick the Grafted's death and finish Nepheli Loux's questline, because his late-game shop stock depends on her story reaching its end.
name: Gatekeeper Gostoc's questline

steps.text: Gostoc is in the gatehouse to the left of Stormveil's main gate. He offers you a choice between the front door and the side path. Picking "No, I'll use the main entrance" simply opens the gate for you; you can still take the scaffold route afterwards.

In the western part of the castle you walk into a dark room and Gostoc slams the door behind you, shutting you in with a Banished Knight. Grab the Rusty Key from the room and use it on the door to get out.

From here he starts turning up around the castle, and while he is doing so he skims 30 percent of any runes you drop on death inside the dungeon. Talking to him at a hiding spot for the first time earns you a Grace Mimic.
First spot: a ledge above the Stormveil Cliffside grace, which only appears if you entered the castle by the wooden scaffold and doubled straight back.
Second spot: the ground floor of the western wall, which he occupies once you have climbed the ladder past the door the Rusty Key opened.
Third spot: the roof of the chapel where Rogier sits, which he moves to after you have visited the rooftop with the Grafted Scion and come back.
Fourth spot: a wooden platform inside the lift tower, reached with a jump.

To make the stealing stop, talk to him at any of the first three spots and then at the lift-tower platform, then go all the way back down to the gatehouse and talk to him again. He also opens his shop once he has begun following you.
After Godrick the Grafted falls, Gostoc appears in the boss room. Exhaust his dialogue; his shop reopens and, if you skipped the confrontation, he stops taking a cut here anyway.
Finish Nepheli Loux's questline. Gostoc then stands at the back of the Stormveil throne room, and after his last conversation his shop stocks an Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone for 20,000 runes.

rewardNames: (an Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone on sale for 20,000 runes)
rewardNotes: an Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone on sale for 20,000 runes

missables.trigger: killing Gostoc
missables.lost: the Grace Mimic, his shop and the Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone are gone, and Nepheli Loux's questline can no longer be completed either.

missables.trigger: turning Gostoc hostile without killing him
missables.lost: he stops trading and blocks Nepheli's ending until you buy an Absolution at the Church of Vows with Celestial Dew.

missables.trigger: never completing Nepheli Loux's questline
missables.lost: step 10 never happens, so the 20,000-rune stone never reaches his stock.

desc: The Grandam is a blind old hornsent woman shut in a storeroom in Belurat, the ruined tower settlement you clear in the expansion's opening hours. She has spent her whole life hating Marika's crusade, so the first time you speak to her she takes you for one of Messmer's soldiers and dares you to finish the job. Wear the head of the sacred beast that guards the top of her settlement and she changes completely: you become the vessel of her people's guardian, she teaches you a spirit-calling incantation, and she starts cooking for you. The whole line is short, front-loaded, and easy to lose, because it has to be underway before you burn Messmer down.
whatItIs: Hornsent Grandam is a blind old hornsent woman shut in a storeroom in Belurat, and she has spent her whole life hating Marika's crusade. The first time she is spoken to she assumes the speaker serves Messmer and dares them to finish the job, but wearing the Divine Beast Head changes her attitude completely.
whyItMatters: She teaches the Watchful Spirit incantation and cooks unlimited Scorpion Stew, which trades for Furnace Visages with her son at the plateau crossroads. The line is lost if Shadow Keep is entered or Messmer the Impaler is defeated before the quest is underway, and her final Gourmet Scorpion Stew only appears after the crusade's commander is dead.
whenToUse: Available in the Shadow of the Erdtree content. Find the storeroom key in the drainage channel below the Small Private Altar in Belurat, then kill the Divine Beast Dancing Lion at the theatre on top of the tower settlement and equip its head. Return to the storeroom and speak to her again before entering Shadow Keep or defeating Messmer the Impaler, because either action closes the line.
name: Hornsent Grandam's questline

steps.text: From the small altar grace inside Belurat, head north-west past the omen knight and turn right before the drop beside the waterfall.
Take the alley on your left, kill the two oversized shadow undead, follow the drainage channel to the room on the right and climb the ladder inside for the storeroom key.
Go back up to the raised walkway above the settlement's main avenue and unlock the storeroom door.
(Optional) Speak to the Grandam as you are. She cannot see you, assumes you serve Messmer, and tells you to get on with killing her.
Climb to the theatre at the top of Belurat and kill the Divine Beast Dancing Lion. It leaves behind the Divine Beast Head.
Equip the Divine Beast Head, return to the storeroom and speak to her again. She hears the beast in the room and gives you the Watchful Spirit incantation.
Rest at a grace, then talk to her once more. She hands over a bowl of Scorpion Stew, and will refill it whenever you ask.
Carry a stew to her son, the vengeful hornsent camped at the plateau crossroads. He trades you three furnace visages for his mother's cooking.

lockouts.name: Shadow Keep
lockouts.note: the charm on Miquella's followers breaks, her son leaves the crossroads, and the stew can no longer reach him

steps.text: Push through the keep and kill Messmer the Impaler.

lockouts.name: Messmer the Impaler
lockouts.note: the questline has to be underway already or her final stew never appears

steps.text: Go back to the storeroom one last time. With the crusade's commander dead she cooks the good version, Gourmet Scorpion Stew, and gives it to you freely.

missables.trigger: entering Shadow Keep
missables.lost: the charm on Miquella's followers breaks, her son leaves the crossroads, and the stew can no longer reach him.

missables.trigger: defeating Messmer the Impaler
missables.lost: the questline has to be underway already or her final stew never appears.

desc: The Hornsent is the last son of the people Messmer burned out of these lands, and he is only walking with Miquella's followers because their road happens to point at his enemy. He never pretends to like you, but he hands over the maps of Miquella's crosses that make the Land of Shadow navigable, and he is the ally you want inside Messmer's arena. His thread ends in a duel no matter what you do, so the real question is whether you fight him early on Leda's behalf or late on his own terms; the second route gives you his help against Messmer and one extra ash of war along the way.
whatItIs: The Hornsent is the last son of the people Messmer burned out of these lands, and he is walking with Miquella's followers only because their road points at his enemy. He hands over the Cross Map that makes the Land of Shadow navigable, and his thread ends in a duel no matter what route is taken.
whyItMatters: The rewards include the Falx, his full armour set, Ash of War: Swift Slash, and Leda's Rune, while his gold sign is available for the Golden Hippopotamus and Messmer the Impaler fights. Siding with Needle Knight Leda at the Shadow Keep rampart forfeits the ash of war, the rune, and his help against Messmer, while siding with him forfeits the Lacerating Crossed-Tree and the Sir Ansbach ambush.
whenToUse: Opens only in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Meet him beside Freyja at Three-Path Cross in the Gravesite Plain, then follow him to Highroad Cross in Scadu Altus once the plateau is open. The camp-side choice at the Main Gate Plaza rampart and the duel at the Church of the Bud both require Messmer the Impaler to still be alive, so finish every conversation at the cross before pushing into the keep.
name: The Hornsent's questline

steps.text: Find the Hornsent sitting beside Freyja at Three-Path Cross, on the north side of the plain. Exhaust him and he gives you the Cross Map, which marks three of Miquella's crosses in your Info tab.

Optional: hand him a Scorpion Stew for three Furnace Visages and a story about what Messmer's crusade did to his people. The stew comes from the Hornsent Grandam in Belurat once you speak to her wearing the Divine Beast Head. He only accepts one.

lockouts.name: the burning of the Sealing Tree at Church of the Bud
lockouts.note: the exchange, since he stops being reachable outside combat

steps.text: Reach Scadu Altus by beating Rellana, Twin Moon Knight or by taking the sealed spiritspring behind the Fort of Reprimand, then talk to him at Highroad Cross. He gives the New Cross Map and points out the misshapen umbral tree on the horizon.
Walk the road north to the keep's gates. The message about the shattered rune is what frees him to go after Messmer, so finish every conversation on the cross before you trigger it.
Return to Highroad Cross. He now talks about taking his revenge inside the keep; exhaust him, then reload the area and he is gone.
Optional: his gold sign, next to Freyja's, waits outside the Golden Hippopotamus arena at the top of the entrance lift.

lockouts.name: Golden Hippopotamus
lockouts.note: his cooperator sign for that fight

steps.text: Speak to Leda at Highroad Cross and let her pick a suspect. Whether you name the Hornsent or say nothing, rest at the grace and talk again until she states plainly that she means to be rid of him; that line is what spawns the signs.

From Main Gate Plaza take the left-hand exit, go up the stairs and through the archer's room to the rampart of burning boats. Answer the GOLD sign to fight for the Hornsent, and kill Leda before she kills him, for Ash of War: Swift Slash and Leda's Rune.

lockouts.name: Messmer the Impaler (Messmer + Base Serpent)
lockouts.note: his duel with Leda never happens

steps.text: Fight your way to Messmer at the top of the Specimen Storehouse. His gold sign only appears once the battle has started, near the middle of the arena on your right; summon him.
With Messmer dead, rest at the grace in his chamber and the Hornsent turns up beside it. Exhaust him.
Make your way to the Church of the Bud. He invades on the rot-choked staircase inside; beat him and he leaves the Falx and every piece of his gear.
If you never ran the long route, or never summoned him against Messmer, he simply stands with Leda in the Cleansing Chamber Anteroom instead, and drops exactly the same gear when the group falls.

missables.lost: his cooperator sign for that fight.

missables.trigger: before defeating Messmer the Impaler (Messmer + Base Serpent)
missables.lost: his duel with Leda never happens, so neither the ash of war nor the rune is ever offered.

missables.trigger: siding with Needle Knight Leda at the Shadow Keep rampart
missables.lost: Ash of War: Swift Slash, Leda's Rune and his help against Messmer. You get the Lacerating Crossed-Tree from Leda instead.

missables.trigger: siding with the Hornsent at the Shadow Keep rampart
missables.lost: the Lacerating Crossed-Tree, and the later ambush on Sir Ansbach, since Leda drops that hunt.
