desc: Igon is the ruined dragon hunter you can hear screaming long before you find him, propped against the rocks north-east of the Gravesite Plain with one leg gone and nothing left but hatred for a dragon called Bayle. His quest is short and almost entirely a journey: dig through a cave, cross the foothills, climb a storm-lashed mountain, and summon his spirit for the fight he could not finish alone. Beating Bayle the Dread with Igon at your side is the single most quotable moment in the expansion, and it pays out his greatbow, his armour, his bell bearing and the dragon's heart. Bayle is entirely optional, so nothing in the main story can rush you off this mountain.
whatItIs: Igon is a ruined dragon hunter propped against the rocks north-east of the Gravesite Plain with one leg gone and nothing left but hatred for a dragon called Bayle. His quest is almost entirely a journey: dig through a cave, cross the foothills, climb a storm-lashed mountain, and summon his spirit for the fight he could not finish alone.
whyItMatters: Beating Bayle the Dread with Igon summoned pays out Igon's Greatbow, Ash of War: Igon's Drake Hunt, his full armour set, his bell bearing, and the Heart of Bayle. A kill with no Igon summoned costs the Ash of War: Igon's Drake Hunt permanently, and killing him at either resting spot forfeits the same reward.
whenToUse: Requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion to access. Head to the Pillar Path Waypoint on the Gravesite Plain where a ruined hunter calls out from the rocks, then clear the Dragon's Pit and climb the Jagged Peak to reach his arena at the summit. The boss fight is entirely optional and the main story never forces the ascent, so the line can be picked up whenever the mood strikes.
name: Igon's questline

steps.text: Rest at the waypoint on the pillar road in the north-east of the plain and follow the screaming down the slope to a broken man wedged in the rocks.
Talk to Igon. He is too deep in his own agony to hold a conversation, but the meeting has to happen before the rest of the line will fire.
Head south-south-west from the same grace to the cave mouth at the end of the pillar road and go in.
Work down through the beastman bones and past the magma wyrm to the bottom of the chasm, then kill the Ancient Dragon-Man who guards the exit.
Step out of the cave into the foothills under the mountain and light the grace there.

(Optional) Visit the altar in the shadow of the dead drake and hear the Dragon Communion Priestess out. She explains why the hunt exists and will give you an Ancient Dragon's Blessing whenever you do not already hold one.
Kill the drake that lands in the foothills on the way to the ascent.
Igon is now sitting in the middle of the road onward, laughing instead of screaming. Talk to him until he runs out of lines and hands over his furled finger.
Climb the mountainside through the red lightning, the drake pair and Ancient Dragon Senessax, lighting the graces as you pass them.
Rest at the last grace below the roost, then walk into the open arena at the peak.

Summon Igon from his sign by the arena entrance and fight Bayle the Dread. On a first, never-attempted run the sign only appears once the dragon has crashed down, so wait for him rather than pushing straight in.

lockouts.name: Bayle the Dread
lockouts.note: a kill with no Igon summoned costs you the Ash of War: Igon's Drake Hunt permanently

steps.text: Bayle drops the Heart of Bayle instead of a remembrance, and a grace appears in his roost.

Walk back down to the foothills where the first drake fell. Igon's body is there with his greatbow, all four pieces of his armour, his bell bearing and, if he was summoned for the kill, the ash of war named after his hunt.
Take the heart to the altar in the foothills and gorge on it to choose between Bayle's Flame Lightning and Bayle's Tyranny.

rewardNames: Ash of War: Igon's Drake Hunt

missables.trigger: defeating Bayle the Dread
missables.lost: a kill with no Igon summoned costs you the Ash of War: Igon's Drake Hunt permanently.

missables.trigger: killing Igon yourself at either of his resting spots
missables.lost: the ash of war is forfeit, and killing him on the Gravesite Plain also costs you his furled finger and any chance of summoning him.

desc: This is the first quest most players meet that they cannot win. Irina is a blindfolded girl sitting by the Bridge of Sacrifice who asks you to carry a letter to her father, the castellan holding Castle Morne against a servant uprising. You can deliver it, you can save the castle, you can free the old man from his duty, and she still dies before he reaches her. What the chain actually gives you is the Grafted Blade Greatsword, a talisman on the first hello, a later invasion that pays out, and the opening of Lightseeker Hyetta's story in Liurnia.
whatItIs: Irina of Morne sits blindfolded by the Bridge of Sacrifice asking a passing Tarnished to carry a letter to her father, the castellan holding out at Castle Morne. The chain runs through saving the castle, freeing Edgar from his duty, and ends with his vengeful invasion at the Revenger's Shack.
whyItMatters: It pays out the Grafted Blade Greatsword, a Sacrificial Twig, a Banished Knight's Halberd, and opens Lightseeker Hyetta's questline in Liurnia of the Lakes. It is easy to break: resting at a Site of Grace in Liurnia of the Lakes after taking Irina's Letter kills her instantly, and defeating the Leonine Misbegotten before delivering the letter strands Edgar at his post forever.
whenToUse: Start it in the Weeping Peninsula on the first visit to that region, before ever entering Liurnia of the Lakes. Meet Irina at the Bridge of Sacrifice, deliver the letter to Edgar at Castle Morne Rampart, kill the Leonine Misbegotten with him summoned if desired, and exhaust his dialogue before touching any grace in Liurnia.
name: Irina and Edgar's questline

steps.text: Irina is sitting on a rock beside the road near the Bridge of Sacrifice grace. Talk to her twice and choose to deliver the letter to receive Irina's Letter.
Ride south to Castle Morne and fight up to the tower where Castellan Edgar is holding out. Your first conversation with him earns a Sacrificial Twig, which saves your runes on death.

lockouts.name: Liurnia of the Lakes
lockouts.note: once you rest at a grace in Liurnia after taking the letter, Irina dies whether or not you ever reached Castle Morne

steps.text: Choose "Deliver Irina's Letter". Edgar explains that the rebels have taken the castle's treasured sword, and his summon sign appears at the boss fog.

lockouts.name: Leonine Misbegotten
lockouts.note: the letter has to reach him while the boss is still alive, or his half of the story never starts

steps.text: Go down through the ruined castle to the cliff terrace and kill the Leonine Misbegotten, with Edgar summoned if you want the help. It drops the Grafted Blade Greatsword, the sword he was guarding.
Return to Edgar and exhaust his dialogue. Released from his duty, he sets off to collect his daughter and spend what is left of his life with her.
Ride back to Irina's rock. She is dead, and Edgar is standing over the body. Exhaust his dialogue; he swears to hunt down everything that had a hand in it.

Much later, approach the Revenger's Shack on the western shore of the lake. Edgar invades as Edgar the Revenger, now consumed by the Flame of Frenzy. Kill him for the Banished Knight's Halberd and a Shabriri Grape.
Because Irina died, Lightseeker Hyetta now appears at the Lake-Facing Cliffs grace, wearing Irina's face. Speaking to her starts a separate questline.

missables.trigger: entering Liurnia of the Lakes and resting at a Site of Grace after taking Irina's Letter
missables.lost: Irina dies immediately, Edgar never leaves Castle Morne under his own steam, and the letter delivery is wasted.

missables.trigger: defeating Leonine Misbegotten before handing Edgar the letter
missables.lost: he stays at his post, so the reunion scene at the Bridge of Sacrifice and the Revenger's Shack invasion never happen.

missables.trigger: killing Irina before taking the letter from her
missables.lost: she drops it, but Lightseeker Hyetta will never appear, closing off her entire questline. Some players do this deliberately to soak a Lord of Blood's Favor in her blood.

missables.trigger: killing Edgar in Castle Morne
missables.lost: the Grafted Blade Greatsword can still be taken from the boss, but the rest of his story, including the Revenger invasion, is gone.

desc: Jar-Bairn is a knee-high living jar in the hidden village of Jarburg, hunting for someone smooth- handed enough to be the village's next Potentate. He is the closing chapter of two other stories: Knight Diallos comes here to be that Potentate and dies defending the place from poachers, and Alexander, Warrior Jar, whom the little one calls uncle, leaves behind the keepsake that sets him on the road himself. The quest asks for nothing but patience, a lot of resting at the grace, and one item carried down from Crumbling Farum Azula.
whatItIs: Jar-Bairn is a knee-high living jar in the hidden village of Jarburg who is searching for a smooth-handed successor to become the village Potentate. The story weaves in Knight Diallos and Alexander, Warrior Jar, and closes with the little jar leaving to become a warrior.
whyItMatters: The reward is the Companion Jar, a spirit summon that drops nowhere else in the game. The line breaks if Knight Diallos is never pushed to the point where he leaves Volcano Manor, if Alexander, Warrior Jar's duel at the Dragon Temple Lift is never run, or if Jar-Bairn or any villager is killed.
whenToUse: Begin it after reaching Liurnia of the Lakes and finding Jarburg down the ravine in eastern Liurnia. Push Knight Diallos's chain far enough that he walks out of Volcano Manor, complete Alexander, Warrior Jar's duel near the Dragon Temple Lift, and bring the Alexander's Innards back to Jarburg to finish the line.
name: The little jar of Jarburg

steps.text: Ride down the ravine into Jarburg and find him sitting in front of a house north-west of the grace. Talk him out; he inspects your hands and decides you are too rough to be Potentate. Accepting or refusing his request changes nothing later.
Rest at the village grace and speak to him again for the next batch of dialogue, including his standing invitation to pick the rare flowers growing between the houses.
If you have already run into Alexander, Warrior Jar out in the world, rest once more and he will bring up his uncle and the line about the path of champions being walked alone.
Reload the area and speak to him again to hear him warn you about poachers. This conversation only opens once Knight Diallos has arrived at Volcano Manor.
Carry Diallos's own questline far enough that he gives up on revenge and walks out of Volcano Manor.
Go back to Jarburg and talk to Jar-Bairn about the man who has turned up. He is unimpressed by the knight's strength but very impressed by his hands.

Rest and reload six times, then find the little jar near the centre of the village and speak to him. Talk to Diallos afterwards, reload once more, and speak to Jar-Bairn again to reach the aftermath of the poacher raid, which leaves Diallos dying and several jars broken.
Accept Alexander's duel on the platform near the Dragon Temple Lift grace, beat him, and take Alexander's Innards from the wreckage.
Bring the innards down to Jarburg and give them to Jar-Bairn. He takes them as a promise rather than a gift and decides to leave the village to become a warrior.
Exhaust his dialogue, then rest and reload. He is gone, and the Companion Jar is sitting where he used to sit.

missables.trigger: completing step 8 (winning Alexander's duel in Crumbling Farum Azula)
missables.lost: Alexander's Innards only drop there, so any break in his chain of meetings also costs you the Companion Jar.

missables.trigger: completing step 5 (Knight Diallos leaving Volcano Manor)
missables.lost: if his own questline is never pushed that far, Jar-Bairn's dialogue stalls at the poacher warning and the ending never arrives.

missables.trigger: killing Jar-Bairn or the villagers
missables.lost: the line ends immediately, and the Companion Jar cannot be obtained any other way.

desc: Kenneth Haight is a loud, self-important noble standing on a ruin in eastern Limgrave who insists he is the rightful ruler of the region and would very much like someone else to win it back for him. His quest is short, entirely contained in Limgrave, and it is the cleanest excuse a new player has to clear Fort Haight, a garrison worth emptying on its own merits. Its ending is not really his own: it only closes once Nepheli Loux takes the throne at Stormveil, and Kenneth turns up to bend the knee to her.
whatItIs: Kenneth Haight stands on a ruin in eastern Limgrave insisting he is the rightful lord and begging someone to win back Fort Haight for him. His story is short, stays entirely in Limgrave, and only closes once Nepheli Loux takes the throne at Stormveil Castle.
whyItMatters: The reward is the Erdsteel Dagger and a cleared Fort Haight, plus the throne-room ending scene. Killing Kenneth at any point loses both the dagger and the finale, and skipping Nepheli Loux's questline leaves his story stuck at a deflated speech with no resolution.
whenToUse: Pick it up in the first hours while still in Limgrave, east of the Artist's Shack and west of the Third Church of Marika. Clear Fort Haight West to earn the dagger, then park the quest and finish Nepheli Loux's chain before returning to the Stormveil throne room for the closing scene.
name: Kenneth Haight's questline

steps.text: Find Kenneth standing on top of a ruined structure in eastern Limgrave, east of the Artist's Shack and west of the Third Church of Marika. You can also reach him by riding north from Mistwood Outskirts. Agree to retake his fort.
Ride south-east to Fort Haight and fight your way to the top of the keep. The blood-obsessed Godrick Knight holding the fort is the enemy you have to put down.
Return to Kenneth on his ruin. He hands over the Erdsteel Dagger and offers to knight you, telling you to meet him at the fort for the ceremony.

Go back to Fort Haight and speak to him there. Seeing the state of the place deflates him; he decides Limgrave needs a lord of proper lineage and admits he no longer has the standing to knight anyone.
Put his quest on hold and complete Nepheli Loux's questline instead, all the way to the point where she and Gatekeeper Gostoc appear in the Stormveil throne room.

Return to Stormveil Castle and walk past the Godrick the Grafted grace into the throne room. Kenneth is there beside Nepheli, having found the lord he was looking for, and promises to make good on your knighthood once he is back at his fort.

missables.trigger: killing Kenneth at any point
missables.lost: the Erdsteel Dagger reward and the throne-room ending are both lost, though he drops a Golden Seed in exchange.

missables.trigger: never completing Nepheli Loux's questline
missables.lost: step 6 never becomes available, so his story stops at the deflated speech in the ruined fort.

desc: Bernahl runs the Warmaster's Shack in Limgrave, which is where most players buy their first ashes of war, and he is easy to write off as a shopkeeper. He is actually a fallen Tarnished champion who lost his Finger Maiden and went over to Volcano Manor, and his questline is the Recusant contract chain seen from a comrade's side: he sells you better and better ashes as you assassinate people for Tanith, fights beside you in Leyndell and Crumbling Farum Azula, and then invades and tries to kill you. It has one brutal trap - killing Rykard the fast way, before Bernahl ever moves, skips the entire quest.
whatItIs: Behind the ashes-of-war shop at the Warmaster's Shack, Knight Bernahl is a fallen champion who defects to Volcano Manor and becomes a co-conspirator in a chain of assassinations for Tanith. The questline ends with his invasion as a Recusant near the Great Bridge in Crumbling Farum Azula.
whyItMatters: It hands over Gelmir's Fury, the Blasphemous Claw, the Raging Wolf Set, and two ashes of war (Ash of War: Eruption and Ash of War: Assassin's Gambit) through the Twin Maiden Husks. A major trap is reaching Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy before Bernahl has relocated: the whole chain stays locked at the Warmaster's Shack and his drops never move.
whenToUse: Talk to him at the Warmaster's Shack north of the Gatefront Ruins in the first few hours, then pick up Volcano Manor contracts at a comfortable pace before riding to Leyndell or Crumbling Farum Azula. Do not defeat Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy until Bernahl has handed over Gelmir's Fury and left the Manor for good.
name: Bernahl's questline

steps.text: Speak to Bernahl at the Warmaster's Shack, north of the Gatefront Ruins. However you answer his question, his ashes of war shop opens.

lockouts.name: Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy
lockouts.note: if you kill Rykard early by riding the Abductor Virgin out of Raya Lucaria, Bernahl never moves to Volcano Manor and his whole questline is skipped; his drops appear at the Warmaster's Shack instead

steps.text: Talk to Tanith inside Volcano Manor and pick "Join Volcano Manor" to receive the Drawing-Room Key. Bernahl relocates to the eastern quarter of the manor, the same wing where Rya the Scout is found.

Take the first Letter from Volcano Manor and go assassinate Old Knight Istvan. Come back and speak to Bernahl: his shop now carries everything he sold in Limgrave plus Ash of War: Eruption and Ash of War: Assassin's Gambit.
Take the second contract and assassinate Rileigh the Idle. Speak to Bernahl again and he hands you the Letter to Bernahl, asking you to join him on a hunt of his own.

Go to the Fortified Manor in Leyndell and find the invasion sign on the first floor, in front of the corpse holding the Alberich's Set. Use it to be pulled in on Bernahl's side against Vargram the Raging Wolf and Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm.
Winning that double assassination pays out Vargram's Raging Wolf Set.
Return to Bernahl in Volcano Manor. He gives you Gelmir's Fury for the job, and this is also what puts his summon sign in Crumbling Farum Azula.
Kill Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, then exhaust Bernahl's dialogue one last time. He leaves the Manor for good, though his shop stays open through the "Sword of Bernahl" left on his chair.
Bernahl's gold summon sign appears near the Dragon Temple grace. Call him in for the Godskin Duo fight - he is one of the better NPC summons in the endgame.
Follow the path north from the Great Bridge. Just before the tower holding the chest with the Old Lord's Talisman, Bernahl invades you as a Recusant. Kill him for the Blasphemous Claw.
Keep the Blasphemous Claw - using it to parry Maliketh, the Black Blade's Destined Death attacks is the whole reason that fight has a difficulty setting.

missables.trigger: before defeating Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy
missables.lost: if you reach and kill Rykard by riding the Abductor Virgin out of the Academy of Raya Lucaria before Bernahl has relocated to Volcano Manor, he never moves at all. His drops are left at the Warmaster's Shack and the entire questline, Gelmir's Fury and the Raging Wolf Set included, is skipped.

missables.trigger: before completing step 4
missables.lost: the Letter to Bernahl only comes after the Rileigh the Idle contract, and without it the Fortified Manor invasion sign against Vargram the Raging Wolf and Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm never appears.

missables.trigger: before completing step 7
missables.lost: Bernahl's summon sign for the Godskin Duo only exists if you have already been rewarded with Gelmir's Fury for the Leyndell hunt.

missables.trigger: Handing Bernahl's Bell Bearing to the Twin Maiden Husks before you have the Drawing-Room Key means their stock will never include Ash of War
missables.lost: Eruption or Ash of War: Assassin's Gambit; give it to them afterwards instead.

missables.trigger: Killing Bernahl at the Warmaster's Shack is the only way to get Bernahl's Bell Bearing, and doing so ends his questline before it starts.

desc: Diallos is the loud, useless younger brother of a famous warrior house, and his quest is the game's quietest redemption arc. He starts by asking every stranger in Roundtable Hold whether they have seen his missing servant, swears vengeance when he finds her dead, joins the people who killed her instead, and then walks away from all of it to look after a village of clay pots. Following him means checking in on him at four different places across dozens of hours, so it is easy to lose track of - and it only finishes if you also push Jar-Bairn's story along in Jarburg.
whatItIs: Knight Diallos roams Roundtable Hold asking strangers about his missing servant, swears vengeance when she is found dead, then abandons that revenge to join the very people he blamed. The arc ends in Jarburg where he dies defending the village of clay pots from poachers.
whyItMatters: The rewards are Hoslow's Petal Whip and Diallos's Mask, both dropped where he falls in Jarburg. The line breaks if Jar-Bairn's quest is never pushed to the point where Diallos can relocate there, and it also requires one of Tanith's contracts to be finished or Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy to be slain before Diallos will leave Volcano Manor.
whenToUse: He appears in Roundtable Hold on the very first arrival, so listen to him then. Follow him through Liurnia at the Academy Gate Town, join Volcano Manor, finish a contract, and check Jarburg in eastern Liurnia after he has made the move there.
name: Diallos's questline

steps.text: Optional first meeting: Diallos is standing in Roundtable Hold the first time you arrive. Talk to him and he asks you to keep an eye out for Lanya, his servant, who has wandered off.
Diallos turns up in Liurnia, just north of the Academy Gate Town grace. He has found Lanya dead and blames the recusants of Volcano Manor. Exhaust everything he says.
He goes back to Roundtable Hold. Speak to him and he tells you where Volcano Manor is - this is one of the ways players first learn the place exists.
Join the Recusants under Tanith and Diallos appears in the Volcano Manor drawing room. He has taken her flattery and abandoned the revenge he swore.

Either complete one of Tanith's assassination contracts or kill Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, then speak to Diallos again in the drawing room and exhaust his dialogue. He has worked out that he was played.

Push Jar-Bairn's story along at Jarburg, in eastern Liurnia. Once Diallos has left Volcano Manor he relocates there as the village's new "Potentate" and spends his days looking after the living jars. Talk to him.
Rest at a Site of Grace five times, then come back to Jarburg. Jar-poachers have raided the village and Diallos is dying of the wounds he took holding them off.
Speak to him and tell him the jars are safe, then reload the area to collect Diallos's Mask and Hoslow's Petal Whip from where he fell.

missables.trigger: before completing step 6
missables.lost: Diallos never moves to Jarburg unless Jar-Bairn's questline has been progressed there, so a player who never visits Jarburg simply loses the end of his story and both rewards.

missables.trigger: before completing step 5
missables.lost: Diallos only leaves Volcano Manor after you have either finished one of Tanith's contracts or killed Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, and spoken to him about it.

missables.trigger: Killing Diallos at any point gives the same two items but ends the questline on the spot, so his Jarburg chapters are lost.

desc: Latenna is a crippled Albinauric archer whose wolf was killed by Gideon Ofnir's servants while they were trying to beat the location of the Haligtree medallion out of her. She will not tell you anything until you prove you already have the other half. Her quest is really the map route to Miquella's Haligtree, and the spirit ash she becomes is one of the best ranged summons in the game - she stands still, shoots constantly and never chases. The catch is a sequencing trap: pick the medallion halves up in the wrong order and she dies before you ever speak to her.
whatItIs: Latenna the Albinauric is a crippled archer sheltered in the Slumbering Wolf's Shack who will not speak until she sees proof that one half of a secret medallion has already been found. Her story is the route into the Consecrated Snowfield and onward to the Haligtree.
whyItMatters: She becomes a stationary ranged spirit ash that fires constantly without chasing, and also drops a Somber Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone at the Apostate Derelict. The sequencing trap is real: taking the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Left) from Castle Sol before ever speaking to her means she is already dead by the time the shack is reached.
whenToUse: Start it in Liurnia of the Lakes after clearing the Lakeside Crystal Cave, carrying the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Right) obtained from Old Albus in the Village of the Albinaurics. Do not enter Castle Sol until after speaking to Latenna at the Slumbering Wolf's Shack, then finish her dialogue at the Apostate Derelict in the Consecrated Snowfield.
name: Latenna's questline

steps.text: Go to the Village of the Albinaurics in the far south-west of Liurnia and work your way to the bottom of it. One of the pots down there is Old Albus in disguise - hit it to break the disguise, then talk to him and take the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Right).
Clear the Lakeside Crystal Cave, on the west shore of the lake. The exit at the far end of it is the only way onto the ledge above.

Follow the path out of the cave to the Slumbering Wolf's Shack and speak to Latenna inside, carrying the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Right). She tells you where the other half is, then gives herself up so you can carry her - she dies, and you pick up Latenna the Albinauric as a spirit ash where she sat.

lockouts.name: step 5
lockouts.note: if you take the left medallion from Castle Sol first, Latenna is already dead when you arrive and you get the ashes without a single line of her dialogue

steps.text: Latenna speaks up on her own when you get near Castle Sol in the north of the Mountaintops, telling you the medallion is close.
Fight through Castle Sol, kill Commander Niall, and carry on past his arena to pick up the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Left).
Take both halves to the Grand Lift of Rold and use the secret medallion option instead of the normal one. The lift drops you into the Consecrated Snowfield.
Cross the snowfield to the Apostate Derelict, right at the northern edge, and approach the sleeping giant Albinauric woman there. Latenna appears beside her to hand over the birthing droplet.
Exhaust Latenna's dialogue at the Apostate Derelict. She asks to be laid to rest beside her wolf when the fighting is done, and leaves you a Somber Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone.

missables.trigger: before completing step 5
missables.lost: taking the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Left) from Castle Sol before speaking to Latenna means she is already dead at the Slumbering Wolf's Shack. Her spirit ash is still there, but every line of her dialogue and the whole meeting is lost.

missables.trigger: before completing step 3
missables.lost: without the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Right) from Old Albus in the Village of the Albinaurics, Latenna refuses to talk and the quest cannot start.

missables.trigger: before completing step 8
missables.lost: the Somber Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone only appears if you carry Latenna as a spirit ash all the way to the Apostate Derelict and finish her dialogue there.

desc: Hyetta is a blind woman walking north through Liurnia towards a light only she can see, asking passing strangers for grapes. The grapes are human eyes, the light is the Three Fingers, and her quest is the game's route to the Frenzied Flame - so it ends by offering you the single most destructive decision in Elden Ring. She only exists at all if Irina of Morne has already died, and the last step permanently overwrites your ending unless you undo it later, so read the missables before you finish it.
whatItIs: Lightseeker Hyetta is a blind woman walking north through Liurnia collecting grapes that are actually human eyes, all in pursuit of a light she alone can see. Her quest is the route to the Frenzied Flame and ends by presenting a choice that locks the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending if accepted.
whyItMatters: It yields the Frenzied Flame Seal and a Frenzyflame Stone, and opens the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending. Hyetta only spawns if Irina of Morne has died through her own questline rather than being killed directly, and accepting the final embrace at the Frenzied Flame Proscription locks that ending unless Miquella's Needle is used to reverse it.
whenToUse: Start it at the Lake-Facing Cliffs grace on the path down from Stormveil into Liurnia of the Lakes, after Irina of Morne has died through her questline. The chain moves north through the Purified Ruins, the Gate Town Bridge, and Bellum Church before the final descent into the Frenzied Flame Proscription below the capital, which requires Morgott, the Omen King to be defeated first.
name: Hyetta's questline

steps.text: Finish Irina's questline so that Irina of Morne dies. Hyetta will not spawn anywhere in Liurnia while Irina is still alive, and killing Irina yourself does not count.
Hyetta appears near the Lake-Facing Cliffs grace, on the path down from Stormveil into Liurnia. Talk to her and she asks for a Shabriri Grape.
The closest grape is just south of her, inside the rear entrance to Stormveil Castle - the door set into the cliff. Bring it back and give it to her.
She moves north to the Purified Ruins. The second grape is in the cellar of those same ruins, east of where she stands, hidden under wooden planks. Give it to her.

She moves again, to just north of the Gate Town Bridge grace. The third grape is dropped by Edgar the Revenger, who appears outside the Revenger's Shack on the west side of Liurnia, north of the Minor Erdtree, after Irina's questline is over.
After she eats the third grape you get the option to tell her the truth - that the grapes are human eyes. Choose it, hear her out, then reload the area and speak to her again in the same spot.
Hyetta is now inside Bellum Church, north-east across the lake. She asks for a Fingerprint Grape, which only grows on someone the burnt Fingers have clasped.
Go to the Church of Inhibition in the Frenzied Flame Village. Festering Fingerprint Vyke invades you on the approach; kill him for the Fingerprint Grape.
Bring the Fingerprint Grape back to Bellum Church, give it to her and exhaust her dialogue. The light is close enough now that she can follow it herself.

Beat Morgott, the Omen King, then descend into the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds below the capital and go all the way down to the Frenzied Flame Proscription. Hyetta is waiting at the sealed door. Exhaust her dialogue.
STOP HERE unless you have read the missables. To go on you must strip off every piece of armour and interact with the door behind her, which burns the Three Fingers' flame into you.

lockouts.name: step 12
lockouts.note: accepting the flame overwrites your ending with Lord of Frenzied Flame and ends Melina's accord with you, and only Miquella's Needle can reverse it

steps.text: After the cutscene, go back to Hyetta and speak to her twice. She relays the words of the Three Fingers, then burns where she stands, leaving the Frenzied Flame Seal and five Frenzyflame Stone.

missables.trigger: before completing step 2
missables.lost: Hyetta never appears if Irina of Morne is still alive, and she also never appears if you simply murder Irina - Irina must die through her own questline, or by you lighting a grace in Liurnia of the Lakes after taking Irina's Letter.

missables.trigger: before completing step 12
missables.lost: accepting the Frenzied Flame locks your ending to Lord of Frenzied Flame. Melina breaks her accord with you, and you cannot pick any other ending unless you later suppress the flame with Miquella's Needle.

missables.trigger: before completing step 11
missables.lost: you must have no armour equipped in any of the four slots for the door to open, and there is no prompt telling you so.

desc: Melina is the spectral girl who offers to stand in as your Finger Maiden, which is the only reason your runes ever turn into levels, and she hands over the whistle that calls Torrent. Her thread is not optional flavour: it is the spine of the main story. Follow it and you get the horse, the ability to level at all, the medallion that raises the lift into the Mountaintops of the Giants, and finally the burning of the Erdtree that carries you into the endgame. Break it and you lose her for the rest of the run.
whatItIs: Melina is the spectral girl who appears at the Church of Elleh and offers to stand in as the character's Finger Maiden, which is what makes spending runes on levels possible at all. She also hands over the Spectral Steed Whistle that calls Torrent, and her thread runs through the entire main story to the burning of the Erdtree.
whyItMatters: Without her accord there is no leveling, no horse, and no Rold Medallion to reach the Mountaintops of the Giants. She is lost permanently if the Three Fingers embrace at the Frenzied Flame Proscription is accepted, closing every ending except Lord of Frenzied Flame unless Miquella's Needle reverses it.
whenToUse: She arrives at the Church of Elleh after lighting at least two Sites of Grace in the open world, so the first meeting happens within the opening minutes. Carry the thread through the Minor Erdtree Church on Altus Plateau, the Avenue Balcony in the capital, and finally the Forge of the Giants, exhausting all her dialogue before giving the final answer.
name: Melina's accord

steps.text: Light at least two Sites of Grace out in the open world, then sit at one and wait for the screen to dim; Melina steps out of nowhere and offers her accord.
Accept the accord so that runes can be spent on levels, and take the Spectral Steed Whistle she leaves with you, which calls Torrent for the rest of the game.

While they are still on offer, pick the grace options "The Rays of Grace" and "Melina's Goal" to hear who she is and what she wants; both are quiet, optional conversations that stop being offered once the story moves on.

lockouts.name: Melina's invitation to Roundtable Hold
lockouts.note: both conversations are gone unheard

steps.text: Rest at any grace outside Limgrave, or simply walk up to Margit, the Fell Omen once, and then accept her invitation to Roundtable Hold when it appears.
Rest at the Minor Erdtree Church grace and ask her to share the echo of Queen Marika that lingers there; for listening she teaches you the Outer Order gesture.
Rest at any grace inside the capital; Melina says the accord is fulfilled, entrusts you with Torrent and the strength of runes, and leaves, and her grace conversations stop until Morgott is dead.
Optional. Before you step through the fog to Morgott, the Omen King, touch her summon sign outside the arena to bring her in as a cooperator for the only fight she ever helps with.

lockouts.name: Morgott, the Omen King
lockouts.note: the summon sign is gone for this playthrough

steps.text: Kill Morgott, the Omen King, walk up to the thorn-choked entrance of the Erdtree so the game registers that it has turned you away, then go back and rest; Melina returns and gives you the Rold Medallion.
Optional. Ride up past the Grand Lift of Rold and hear Shabriri out; afterwards Melina gains a new plea at graces, begging you not to take the Frenzied Flame.

The fork. Descending through the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds and the Cathedral of the Forsaken, stripping every piece of armour off and opening the sealed door lets the Three Fingers embrace you, which permanently ends the accord and drives Melina away for good.
The intended finish. Kill the Fire Giant, rest at the Forge of the Giants, exhaust everything she still has to say, and only then answer "I'm ready" so she can burn the Erdtree.

lockouts.name: the Three Fingers embrace at Frenzied Flame Proscription
lockouts.note: Melina abandons the accord and this ending closes

missables.trigger: completing the Three Fingers embrace at Frenzied Flame Proscription
missables.lost: Melina ends the accord and leaves permanently, taking her remaining dialogue and her cooperator sign with her, and every ending except Lord of Frenzied Flame closes unless you later carry Miquella's Needle into Dragonlord Placidusax's arena.

missables.trigger: completing Melina's "I'm ready" answer at Forge of the Giants
missables.lost: any line of hers you have not already heard is lost, because the game cuts straight to Crumbling Farum Azula.

missables.trigger: completing Melina's invitation to Roundtable Hold
missables.lost: the optional grace conversations "The Rays of Grace" and "Melina's Goal" stop being offered.

missables.trigger: defeating Morgott, the Omen King
missables.lost: her cooperator sign outside his arena disappears with him.

desc: Kale is the merchant at the ruined church a short ride from where the game drops you, and he is almost certainly the first person in the Lands Between who is glad to see you. He is also the only merchant who sells the Crafting Kit, which is the item that switches the entire crafting system on. His questline is tiny and mostly conversational, but it hides one genuinely missable gesture that is the intended way to start Blaidd's story, so it is worth doing properly on the way past.
whatItIs: A ruined-church merchant a short ride north of the first grace, Merchant Kale is glad to see the Tarnished and offers to trade. He sells the Crafting Kit, the item that switches the entire crafting system on, and his questline includes a gesture that calls Blaidd the Half-Wolf to the Mistwood Ruins.
whyItMatters: The Crafting Kit is cheap here and leaves his stock entirely after the second shardbearer kill, so buying it early avoids a higher price from the Twin Maiden Husks later. The Finger Snap gesture is lost for the run if Altus Plateau is entered before asking him about the howling near Mistwood Ruins, and with it goes the intended way to summon Blaidd the Half-Wolf.
whenToUse: Head to the ruined church on the hill just north of the Church of Elleh grace and buy the Crafting Kit plus his cookbooks early in the run. Ride east to the Mistwood Ruins to hear the howl, then return and ask Kale about it so he teaches the Finger Snap gesture. Every one of those beats has to land before stepping into Altus Plateau, or the gesture and the intended opening of Blaidd's story are gone.
name: Kale's questline

steps.text: Ride north from the first grace to the ruined church on the hill and talk to the man sitting by the fire; he identifies you as Tarnished and offers to trade.
Buy the Crafting Kit from him. It is cheap here and it is the switch that turns on the whole item-crafting menu, so it should be the first serious purchase of the run.

lockouts.name: your second shardbearer kill
lockouts.note: the kit leaves Kale's stock and costs more at the Twin Maiden Husks

steps.text: Pick up the two cheap cookbooks and the Missionary's Cookbook he keeps in stock, which give you the starter recipe list to actually use the kit with.
Buy the Telescope while you are there. It costs little and it lets you scout camps, dragons and item glimmers from a safe ridge, which matters more in the opening hours than any weapon he sells.

Ask him about himself. He explains that his people were spurned by grace, that they cannot settle, and that he considers the Tarnished kindred spirits, then asks you not to harm his kin out on the roads.
Ride east to the Mistwood Ruins and listen for the enormous howl that carries across the forest at that spot.

lockouts.name: Altus Plateau
lockouts.note: the howl stops counting and Kale's gesture is lost

steps.text: Go back and ask Kale about the howling near Mistwood Ruins. He knows exactly who it is, calls him boorish but decent, and teaches you the Finger Snap gesture.

lockouts.name: Altus Plateau
lockouts.note: the gesture can no longer be learned

steps.text: Return to the Mistwood Ruins and perform Finger Snap there to call Blaidd the Half-Wolf down off the ruins, which is the intended opening of his questline and of the help he gives against Darriwil.
Leave him alive. Kale keeps his stock for the whole game and there is no reward for turning on him beyond his bell bearing, which only duplicates what he already sells.
Only if you do kill him, take Kale's Bell Bearing off his body and give it to the Twin Maiden Husks, who will then sell his inventory in his place for the rest of the run.

missables.trigger: entering Altus Plateau before asking Kale about the howling near Mistwood Ruins
missables.lost: the Finger Snap gesture is gone for the run, and with it the intended way to call Blaidd the Half-Wolf at the Mistwood Ruins.

missables.trigger: completing the killing of Merchant Kale before asking about the howling
missables.lost: the gesture dies with him, since only he teaches it.

missables.trigger: completing your second shardbearer kill before buying the Crafting Kit
missables.lost: the kit leaves Kale's stock entirely and has to be bought at a higher price from the Twin Maiden Husks instead.

desc: Millicent is a red-haired swordswoman rotting to death in a church above Sellia, and she carries Malenia's blood. Cure her with a needle of unalloyed gold, hand her a golden arm to replace the one she lost, and she becomes a travelling companion who plants summon signs outside several hard bosses and follows you all the way to the Haligtree. Her last scene forces a choice: stand with her against the four "sisters" who come to kill her, or stand with them. One branch hands you a rot-scaling talisman and the needle that undoes the Frenzied Flame; the other hands you a raw damage talisman and closes the first branch for the whole playthrough.
whatItIs: Millicent is a red-haired swordswoman rotting to death in the Church of the Plague above Sellia, carrying Malenia's blood and awaiting a mended needle of unalloyed gold as her cure. She becomes a travelling companion who plants summon signs outside hard bosses, and her final scene in Elphael forces a choice that splits the rewards in two.
whyItMatters: The rewards split by branch: the gold sign at Elphael gives the Rotten Winged Sword Insignia, the Unalloyed Gold Needle, and Miquella's Needle, while the red sign gives Millicent's Prosthesis and closes the first set for the playthrough. Killing her outside the Elphael summon ends everything, and defeating Godskin Apostle before her summon sign appears there loses the Windmill Village conversation.
whenToUse: Begin it in Caelid after killing Commander O'Neil at the Heart of Aeonia and mending the needle with Sage Gowry, then offer it at the Church of the Plague. The chain then moves through the Erdtree-Gazing Hill, Altus Plateau at the Godskin Apostle arena, the Ancient Snow Valley Ruins, and finally Elphael in the Consecrated Snowfield.
name: Millicent's journey

steps.text: (Optional) Ride into the southern edge of the Swamp of Aeonia and let her red phantom invade. She fights with a Shamshir and opens with Waterfowl Dance, so bait the flurry and punish the recovery.

lockouts.name: step 3
lockouts.note: curing her removes the phantom and this duel can never be triggered again

steps.text: Wade north through the rot to the Heart of Aeonia and kill Commander O'Neil, who leaves a snapped needle of unalloyed gold. Carry it to Sage Gowry in the shack just past the Sellia Gateway on the town's southern edge and let him mend it.
Rest, reload the shack, collect the mended needle, then climb the cliff path east of Sellia to the Church of the Plague and offer the needle to Millicent. She takes it herself and passes out.
Sit at the church grace, wake her, and talk until she thanks you with the Prosthesis-Wearer Heirloom and says she means to leave on a journey.
Go back down to Gowry's shack. She is standing where the old man used to sit, remembering almost nothing of him. Exhaust her farewell.
Find her resting on the rise just north of the Erdtree-Gazing Hill grace and talk her out. She is retracing the road Malenia took after Aeonia and wants a sword arm again.

Push into the Shaded Castle and open the chest in its far north-western corner, watched over by a Cleanrot Knight, to take the Valkyrie's Prosthesis. Hugging the inner wall westward is the cheapest route in.
Bring the golden arm back to her. Once she has it, her summon sign appears outside Godskin Apostle (Altus Plateau), Draconic Tree Sentinel and Black Blade Kindred (Forbidden Lands).
Call her in for the Godskin Apostle (Altus Plateau) at Dominula, win, then speak to her beside the grace outside the arena.

lockouts.name: Godskin Apostle (Altus Plateau)
lockouts.note: kill it without her and her sign never appears, so this conversation is gone

steps.text: She turns up beside the Ancient Snow Valley Ruins grace, hunting the fort that holds the medallion to the hidden tree. Exhaust her dialogue.
Reach Elphael and find her sitting by the Prayer Room grace. Here she admits she is of Malenia's blood without knowing how.
(Optional) Visit Gowry now and he will explain what he wants from you next: side with the sisters and put Millicent down.
Kill the Putrid Tree Spirit in the rot pit below the Prayer Room. Two summon signs, one gold and one red, then appear together on the ledge above the pool.

Branch A - take the GOLD sign to fight beside her against Mary, Maureen, Amy and Polyanna. You are paid the Rotten Winged Sword Insignia, and afterwards she lies by the pool, pulls the needle out herself and dies. Reload and loot the Unalloyed Gold Needle from her body.
Branch B - take the RED sign instead to kill her alongside the four sisters. You are paid Millicent's Prosthesis, an Aeonian Bloom is left in your own world, and Gowry vanishes from his shack.
Branch A only: kill Malenia, Blade of Miquella, reload the arena, and push the recovered Unalloyed Gold Needle into the Scarlet Aeonia that blooms where she fell to receive Miquella's Needle.

missables.trigger: completing step 3 (giving Millicent the mended needle)
missables.lost: the Swamp of Aeonia invasion never triggers again.

missables.trigger: defeating Godskin Apostle (Altus Plateau)
missables.lost: her summon sign outside Dominula never appears, so the conversation at the Windmill Village grace is lost.

missables.trigger: killing Millicent yourself outside the Elphael summon
missables.lost: the whole line ends where you stand, and she leaves no needle behind.

missables.trigger: taking the RED sign at Elphael (step 15)
missables.lost: Rotten Winged Sword Insignia, the Unalloyed Gold Needle and Miquella's Needle are all closed off for this playthrough.

missables.trigger: taking the GOLD sign at Elphael (step 14)
missables.lost: Millicent's Prosthesis is closed off for this playthrough.

desc: Everyone who followed Miquella into the Land of Shadow was held together by a charm, and the moment that charm snaps they start hunting each other. Needle Knight Leda appoints herself judge of who still deserves to stand beside her god; you get to pick who she gets to kill and who she does not, and every one of those choices decides who is waiting at the top of Enir-Ilim with a sword out and who is waiting there with a summon sign. The line ends in a gang fight on the stairs below the Gate of Divinity, and then in the expansion's last boss. This file covers the shared part - the charm breaking, the two assassinations, and the tower - rather than any one follower's own story.
whatItIs: The Miquella's Followers are a band of companions held together by a great rune's charm, and the moment that charm snaps at the Shadow Keep gate they turn on each other. Needle Knight Leda appoints herself judge, and the choices made at each crossroads decide who is alive and loyal at the top of Enir-Ilim.
whyItMatters: The loot is extensive: Leda's Sword, Leda's Armor, Freyja's full set, Ansbach's Longbow and attire, Dane's Hat and weapon, plus talismans and a bell bearing. Entering Shadow Keep breaks every first-stage conversation, and entering Enir-Ilim kills every follower questline still in progress except those of Ymir, Jolan, Queelign, and Igon.
whenToUse: The whole storyline is confined to the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Begin it on the Gravesite Plain after meeting the followers at the crossroads graces, exhaust every one of their friendly dialogues before riding to the Shadow Keep gate, and finish all their individual errands before burning the sealing tree at the Church of the Bud.
name: The Enir-Ilim finale

steps.text: Meet the compatriots first. Leda, the Hornsent and Redmane Freyja gather at one crossroads grace on the plain, Sir Ansbach and Moore at the gate crossroads, and Thiollier alone further north-east.
Exhaust every one of them while the charm still holds. Their friendly dialogue never comes back once it breaks.

lockouts.name: Shadow Keep
lockouts.note: the charm shatters and every follower's first-stage conversation is gone

steps.text: Ride to the great gate on the northern plateau. Getting close is enough: the screen reports that a great rune, and with it a powerful charm, has broken.
Do a lap of the crossroads graces. Everyone now has fresh dialogue and their own agenda, and several of them will not stay put much longer.
Find Leda at the plateau crossroads and let her ask you who among the group is unworthy. Naming the Hornsent, or refusing to name anybody, both point her at him.
Rest, then look for the pair of summon signs inside the keep. One enlists you in Leda's hunting party; the other drops you into her target's world to defend him.

Hunting with Leda kills the Hornsent and leaves his falx, mask and rags on the ground; going back to her afterwards earns the Lacerating Crossed-Tree. Defending him instead earns his ash of war and Leda's Rune, and keeps him summonable against Messmer the Impaler.

lockouts.name: step 7
lockouts.note: whichever of the two you refuse can never be taken on that playthrough

steps.text: Sir Ansbach is holed up in a side room off the storehouse floor. Ask him about Freyja before you hand over the secret rite scroll, or Freyja's own thread stalls.

Leda picks Ansbach as her next target. Killing him alongside her drops his longbow and his whole attire and unlocks the Retaliatory Crossed-Tree from her back at the crossroads; siding with him instead gives you the longbow and Leda's Rune, and keeps him alive for the tower.

lockouts.name: step 9
lockouts.note: whichever of the two you refuse can never be taken on that playthrough

steps.text: Fight through the ruins to the church at their summit and kill Romina, Saint of the Bud.
Burn the sealing tree beyond the church with Messmer's kindling. Every unfinished follower errand ends here, so clear your list before you strike the flame.

lockouts.name: Enir-Ilim
lockouts.note: every follower questline still in progress is dead; only Ymir, Jolán, Queelign and Igon carry on afterwards

steps.text: Enter the unshrouded tower and work down and around its spiral until you reach the anteroom below the gate.
Talk to Leda there. She has worked out that the Erdtree, not Miquella, has been guiding you, and that makes you the last thing standing between her god and divinity.
Before stepping onto the stairs, place any summons you have earned. Ansbach and Thiollier both leave gold signs here if their own stories are finished.

Leda attacks with Dryleaf Dane always beside her, plus Freyja and whichever of the Hornsent and Moore are still alive and still loyal. Fight it as a mob fight: pick off the casters, keep moving, and let your summons hold Leda.
Sweep the stairs afterwards. Leda leaves her sword and armour, Dane his hat and his hand-to-hand weapon, Freyja her greatsword and her four plate pieces, Moore his greatshield and bell bearing.
Climb to the gate and fight Promised Consort Radahn, the last boss of the expansion.
Reload and search the arena. If Ansbach survived to fight beside you, his body sits near the entrance with his robes, his lamina and his own incantation.

desc: Moore is a pest in a suit of corroded green plate who sits outside Belurat selling arrows, pots and crafting stock, and who describes his own life mostly in terms of things he has found for other people. He and his forager brood were left behind when the goddess of rot abandoned them, and he follows Miquella because Miquella offered love to the unloved. When the charm breaks he asks you a question with no kind answer, and every possible reply ends with his death. What varies is how much work it costs you and whether you have to fight him at the top of the tower; the loot is the same either way.
whatItIs: Moore sits in corroded green plate outside Belurat, Tower Settlement, selling arrows and crafting stock while describing his life mostly in terms of things he has found for other people. He follows Miquella because Miquella offered love to the unloved, and when the charm breaks he asks a question with no kind answer.
whyItMatters: Every possible reply to his question ends with his death; what varies is how much work it costs and whether he appears in the tower fight. The Verdigris set and his Bell Bearing are the same either way, but the Black Syrup errand for Thiollier's Concoction is lost if the Shadow Keep gate is entered before it is completed.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is required for this one. Begin at the Main Gate Cross below the gate into Belurat, Tower Settlement, purchase something from his shop to unlock his dialogue, and track down the forager brood cookbooks on the plateau and along the Cerulean Coast. Wrap it all up before the Shadow Keep gates loom over you, because that rune-break seals the Black Syrup errand permanently.
name: Moore's questline

steps.text: Moore is sitting with Ansbach beside Main Gate Cross, below the gate into Belurat, Tower Settlement. Buy anything at all from his shop so the "Talk to Moore" option unlocks.
Introduce yourself to Thiollier at Pillar Path Cross first, then come back and use "Talk to Moore". He gives you the Black Syrup and asks you to take it to the poisoner.

lockouts.name: Shadow Keep
lockouts.note: the Black Syrup is never offered

steps.text: Deliver the Black Syrup to Thiollier and ask him about it, which earns you a Thiollier's Concoction and closes Moore's errand.

lockouts.name: Thiollier's move to the Garden of Deep Purple
lockouts.note: the delivery, since Thiollier abandons his cross

steps.text: Find the first forager brood on the plateau above the plain, east of Prospect Town. Talking to one always hands over one volume of its cookbook.

Three more sit up here: on the cliff south of the Castle-Lord's Chamber at Castle Ensis looking north over the canyon, at the poison bog past the cave in the Bear Woods overlooking the Shadow Keep watering hole, and on the cliff south of the Church District entrance along the Church District Highroad.
The last of the talkative foragers is on a cliff overlooking the Abyssal Woods, north of the waterfall at the end of the Ellac River.

The forager directly north of the Church of the Crusade will not speak while it is cold. Set a Warming Stone or a Sunwarmth Stone on the ground beside it, rest or reload, and then talk to it for its cookbook.
With that volume in hand, go back to Moore and he adds the seventh and last of the forager cookbooks.

lockouts.name: the choice at Main Gate Cross
lockouts.note: the seventh cookbook, because two of the three answers make him leave

steps.text: Head north to the Shadow Keep gates so the rune-break message triggers. Moore has nothing new to say until it does.
Return to Main Gate Cross. Moore now asks whether the two of you must be sad together, and offers three answers: put it behind you, remain sad forever, or that you do not know.

"Remain sad forever" is the shortest ending. Moore kills himself immediately, and his body is on top of a forager brood on the cliffs directly north of the Church of the Crusade with his whole kit on it.
"Put it behind you" keeps him alive and puts him in Leda's line at the Cleansing Chamber Anteroom, one more body in an already crowded fight. His gear comes off him there.

"I don't know" sends you back out. Kill a forager brood, report to Moore, then kill a second one; he invades on the spot as a red phantom. Beat him for the same set. Never kill a forager before it has given you its cookbook.
However he dies, Moore's Bell Bearing ends up with him or on the spot beside Main Gate Cross where he used to sit. Hand it to the Twin Maiden Husks to buy his stock permanently.

desc: Leda is the door into Shadow of the Erdtree and the spine that every other follower's quest hangs off. She meets you at Miquella's cocoon, tells you to touch the withered arm, and then leads a band of strangers across the Land of Shadow on Miquella's trail. When Miquella throws away his Great Rune the charm holding that band together snaps, and Leda starts hunting the people she no longer trusts - first the Hornsent, then Sir Ansbach. Whose side you take in those two duels decides which talismans you keep, whether Ansbach lives to fight beside you at the end, and how crowded the last ambush in Enir-Ilim is going to be.
whatItIs: Needle Knight Leda stands at Miquella's cocoon in Mohgwyn Palace and is the door into the Land of Shadow, guiding a band of strangers across the expansion on Miquella's trail. When the Great Rune is thrown away the charm snaps and she begins hunting the followers she no longer trusts.
whyItMatters: Whose side is taken in the two duels decides which talismans are kept (Lacerating Crossed-Tree versus Retaliatory Crossed-Tree), whether Ansbach lives to fight at the top of the tower, and how crowded the final ambush in Enir-Ilim is. Her cooperator sign for Rellana, Twin Moon Knight is lost if that boss is defeated before meeting her, and the rampart signs stop appearing after Messmer the Impaler falls if the contracts are unfinished.
whenToUse: Requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion to even exist. Begin at the Cocoon of the Empyrean in Mohgwyn Palace, which unlocks only after defeating Starscourge Radahn and Mohg, Lord of Blood, then resting at the grace in Mohg's arena to reload the room. Touch the withered arm inside the cocoon and Leda will carry the character into the Land of Shadow, opening the full trail through Belurat, Tower Settlement, Castle Ensis, and Scadu Altus.
name: Leda's questline

steps.text: Kill Starscourge Radahn and Mohg, Lord of Blood, then rest at the grace in Mohg's arena so the room reloads. Leda is standing in front of the cocoon; hear her out.
Touch the withered arm inside the cocoon to be carried into the Land of Shadow.
Clear Belurat, Tower Settlement, then take the lift that opens in the Divine Beast Dancing Lion's arena and climb the grand staircase above it to read her first message.
Push through Castle Ensis until you pass a Black Knight and reach one of Miquella's crosses; her second message sits beside it, saying she is bound for the Shadow Keep.
Optional: answer her gold sign outside the door to Rellana, Twin Moon Knight and fight the boss with her. Skipping this does not stall anything.

lockouts.name: Rellana, Twin Moon Knight
lockouts.note: her cooperator sign for that fight

steps.text: Reach Scadu Altus and find Leda beside Highroad Cross north of Castle Ensis. Exhaust her; if you have already met the Hornsent or Dryleaf Dane you can ask about both.

Before you leave this grace, take the Monk's Missive and the May the Best Win gesture off the broken wall and finish the Hornsent's dialogue too. Everything on this cross moves at once in the next step.

lockouts.name: Shadow Keep
lockouts.note: the conversations that are still owed at Highroad Cross

steps.text: Follow the road north until the Shadow Keep looms over you. The rune shatters, the charm with it, and Leda begins doubting the people standing beside her.
Go back to Highroad Cross. Leda asks who among the followers deserves investigating; name the Hornsent, name Thiollier, or say nothing at all.
Rest at the grace and speak to her again until she settles on the Hornsent. She lands on him no matter which answer you gave.

Leave Main Gate Plaza by the left-hand exit, climb the stairs and cross the room with the archer to reach the rampart of burning boats. Two signs wait beside the stairs down: red joins Leda, gold joins the Hornsent.

lockouts.name: Messmer the Impaler (Messmer + Base Serpent)
lockouts.note: the rampart signs stop appearing

steps.text: If you fought for Leda, return to Highroad Cross and talk to her for the Lacerating Crossed-Tree. She then names Sir Ansbach as her next suspect.
Move Ansbach's own quest along until he has settled into the library off the Storehouse, First Floor, then speak to Leda once more so she goes after him.
Return to Ansbach's room and pick a sign again: red kills him for his armour set, gold keeps him alive for the two fights at the top of the tower.
If you fought for Leda a second time, she owes you the Retaliatory Crossed-Tree; go and claim it at her cross.
Carry on with the story until Romina falls and the kindling taken from Messmer can be set to the great tree sealing the way to Enir-Ilim.

Leda and every follower she still commands are waiting in the Cleansing Chamber Anteroom. Summon your allies on the gold signs first, then touch her red sign. Beating the group leaves Leda's Sword and Leda's Armor on her body.

The rest of her armour is the Oathseeker Knight set, hanging on a corpse over the cliff near the Church of Benediction. Follow the cliff south from Main Gate Cross and keep going past Cliffroad Terminus.

desc: Nepheli is a warrior who fights like a Tarnished but never saw the guidance of grace, and her quest is about finding her a purpose after Godrick falls. It is the most tangled NPC chain in the first half of the game because it leans on three other people: Roderika has to become a spirit tuner, Gideon Ofnir has to be talked to twice at the right moments, and Gostoc has to still be alive. Finish it and she takes the throne of Stormveil Castle, which also closes out Kenneth Haight and reopens Gostoc's shop with the best upgrade material in the game.
whatItIs: Nepheli Loux, Warrior is a Tarnished fighter who never received the guidance of grace, and her quest is about finding her a purpose after Godrick the Grafted falls. The chain is tangled because it leans on Roderika becoming a spirit tuner, Gideon Ofnir being spoken to at the right moments, and Gatekeeper Gostoc staying alive.
whyItMatters: Finishing it places Nepheli on the throne of Stormveil Castle, closes out Kenneth Haight, and restocks Gostoc's shop with an Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone. Defeating Godrick before speaking to Nepheli inside Stormveil Castle loses the Arsenal Charm, giving her Seluvis's Potion instead of The Stormhawk King turns her into a puppet and ends the line, and killing Gostoc makes the throne-room scene impossible.
whenToUse: Begin it in Limgrave while still in the first region, by finding her in the side room past the first pair of Stormhawks in Stormveil Castle. Complete Roderika's questline first so she is a working spirit tuner under Hewg, then speak to Gideon Ofnir at the Table of Lost Grace before summoning Nepheli for the Godrick the Grafted fight.
name: Nepheli Loux's questline

steps.text: Complete Roderika's questline up to the point where she sits opposite Smithing Master Hewg as a working spirit tuner. Nepheli's quest cannot finish without it.
Speak to Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing and exhaust everything he says, so that he retreats into his study behind Ensha of the Royal Remains.

Inside Stormveil Castle, follow the path towards the Secluded Cell grace. Past the first pair of Stormhawks, Nepheli is standing in a small side room. Exhaust her dialogue to place her summon sign outside Godrick's fog wall.

lockouts.name: Godrick the Grafted
lockouts.note: if Godrick dies before you have spoken to her here she will never hand over the Arsenal Charm

steps.text: Summon her for the fight against Godrick the Grafted.
Nepheli is now standing just outside Gideon's study. Speak to her to receive the Arsenal Charm.
Find her on the slope leading up into the Village of the Albinaurics in the south-west of the lake. Exhaust her dialogue to place her summon sign past the bridge before the Omenkiller.
Defeat the Omenkiller at the top of the village. She does not have to be summoned for it to count.

Take an Imbued Sword Key (one sits in the chest beside the grace) to The Four Belfries and use the Precipice of Anticipation sending gate. Past the Grafted Scion, open the side door by the chapel and climb to the roof for The Stormhawk King.
With the Omenkiller dead she moves to the bottom of the stairs near Hewg. Talk to her, then speak to Gideon and choose "Nepheli's despair", then return and exhaust her dialogue again.
Give her The Stormhawk King. This is the choice that carries her quest into its last stage.
After Morgott, the Omen King is dead, return to the Godrick the Grafted grace. Gatekeeper Gostoc is there stamping on Godrick's corpse. Exhaust his dialogue and reload the area until he leaves.

Walk through into the Stormveil throne room. Nepheli is on the throne with Gostoc behind her and Kenneth Haight at her side. Exhaust her dialogue for an Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone; Gostoc will now sell one for 20,000 runes.
Optional epilogue: once the Erdtree burns and the city becomes the Ashen Capital, her summon sign appears outside the fog wall for Godfrey, First Elden Lord.

desc: The nomadic merchants are one family scattered across the whole map, sitting alone at campfires with a mule and a stringed instrument, each selling a stock that reflects wherever they happen to be camped. There is no conversation tree and no reward at the end, but treating them as a route rather than as scenery is one of the strongest quality-of-life moves in the game: between them they sell most of the cookbooks, the ammunition, the early armour and the smithing stones you would otherwise be short of. Every one of them also carries a bell bearing that folds their whole stock into the Twin Maiden Husks at Roundtable Hold, which is where the real payoff lives.
whatItIs: The nomadic merchants are a scattered family sitting alone at campfires across the whole map, each selling a stock that reflects wherever they happen to be camped. There is no conversation tree and no ending reward, but treating them as a shopping route rather than scenery covers most of the cookbooks, ammunition, and early armour a new character needs.
whyItMatters: Every merchant carries a bell bearing that folds their entire stock into the Twin Maiden Husks at Roundtable Hold, which is where the real long-term value lives. A bell bearing only contains the inventory the merchant held at the moment of death, so killing one early permanently loses whatever stock they had not yet unlocked.
whenToUse: Start with Merchant Kale at the Church of Elleh and buy the Crafting Kit before the second shardbearer kill, then sweep the camps in Limgrave, the Weeping Peninsula, Liurnia of the Lakes, Caelid, Altus Plateau, Mt. Gelmir, and the Mountaintops of the Giants as each region is reached. Bring every bell bearing to the Twin Maiden Husks as soon as it is found.
name: The merchant circuit and bell bearings
questName: The merchant circuit and bell bearings

steps.text: Start with Merchant Kale at the Church of Elleh, the only merchant who sells the Crafting Kit and the one who explains what his people are and asks you to trade with the rest of them.
Sweep the three open-world camps in Limgrave itself, in the west near the Agheel Lake shore, in the east on the road toward Mistwood, and in the north up by the Saintsbridge road.
Cross the Bridge of Sacrifice and pick up the pair down there: the nomad camped near the Castle Morne rampart and the isolated merchant tucked away in the south of the peninsula.
Work the lake. There is a nomad on the southern lake shore, a second up in northern Liurnia, and an isolated merchant hidden outside the Academy of Raya Lucaria.
Ride the rot. One nomad sits on the northern Caelid highway, another in the south, and the isolated merchant of Greyoll's Dragonbarrow keeps the most expensive and most useful stock of the three.
On the plateau, find the nomad by the Forest-Spanning Greatbridge and the hermit merchant out in the Capital Outskirts near the Leyndell walls.
Take the mountain road and stop at the nomad camped along the Mt. Gelmir climb, who is the only one selling several of the volcano-flavoured goods.
Up in the snow, the hermit merchant sells the late-game stock, including the smithing materials you will want for the last stretch.
Go underground. The abandoned merchant sits alone by the Siofra River, far from the rest of his family.
Deeper still, the hermit merchant of the Ainsel River keeps a camp beside the underground water.
Whenever you find a bell bearing, whether it was dropped by a merchant, hidden in the world or taken off a Bell Bearing Hunter, bring it to the Twin Maiden Husks and hand it over.

Understand the catch before you kill anyone for one. A merchant's bell bearing only carries the stock they were holding at the moment they died, so killing a merchant early permanently shrinks what the Twin Maiden Husks will ever sell you.
Buy from the living merchants first and treat their bell bearings as a convenience, not a shortcut. Kale in particular is worth leaving alive, since nothing in his stock is unique to the bearing.
If you want the bearings anyway, remember Kale's own warning about his kin. There is no in-game penalty beyond losing the campfire itself, but every merchant killed is one less stall on the road.
