desc: Patches has been ambushing players since Demon's Souls and he has not learned a single lesson. In Elden Ring he runs a bandit crew out of Murkwater Cave, jumps you over a treasure chest, surrenders the moment the fight goes badly, and then follows you across three regions selling goods and setting up the occasional cliff. Nothing in his quest is required for anything else, and it is one of the richest gesture hauls in the game: four gestures come from him and from nobody else. The rule that governs the whole thing is simple. Never finish him.
whatItIs: Patches ambushes the character over a treasure chest in Murkwater Cave, surrenders the moment the fight goes badly, and then follows across three regions selling goods and setting up the occasional cliff. Nothing in his quest is required for anything else, and his rewards include the Magma Whip Candlestick, Cloth Garb, Cloth Trousers, and a handful of gestures.
whyItMatters: The Magma Whip Candlestick, the Cloth Garb, the Cloth Trousers, and several gestures are all on the line, and his travelling shop follows the character for the rest of the run. Killing him at any point removes every later stop, the candlestick, the remaining gestures, and the shop all at once, and the Volcano Manor branch closes if Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy is defeated before joining the Recusants.
whenToUse: Open the treasure chest in Murkwater Cave in the Weeping Peninsula and fight him down to surrender rather than to death, which unlocks the whole chain. The Volcano Manor segment requires joining Tanith's service and completing the first contract before the Great Horned Tragoth kill in the Ruin-Strewn Precipice, and the final stop is back at Murkwater Cave after Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy has fallen.
name: Patches the Untethered's questline

steps.text: Go through the golden fog in Murkwater Cave and open the treasure chest in the boss room for the Cloth Garb and Cloth Trousers. Patches drops from the ceiling accusing you of theft.
Fight him down to about half health. He throws down his spear, begs, and grants the Grovel For Mercy gesture. Reload the area and he is trading rather than fighting.
Optional: keep swinging after the surrender and he turns hostile again. If he gets your health low he teaches Extreme Repentance, and performing it in front of him makes him stand down once more.

Optional: come back later for the second chest in his room. It is a trap that dumps you in Mistwood and blocks fast travel until you rest at a grace. Go back and speak to him about it for the Calm Down! gesture.

Patches has moved to the Scenic Isle grace on the eastern lake. He talks up the Abductor Virgin beneath the Academy of Raya Lucaria as a shortcut to the Erdtree, and mentions a woman named Rya who could use help.
Let the Abductor Virgin take you. It does not deliver you to the Erdtree; it drops you in the Subterranean Inquisition Chamber on the far side of the mountain. Clear your way out.
Return to Patches on Scenic Isle to hear him explain himself, and to collect the Calm Down! gesture if you did not get it from the trap chest.
From the First Mt. Gelmir Campsite grace, head west past the siege tower and then north. Patches urges you along a trail of glowstones to a ledge, and kicks you off it.
Climb back and talk to him for the Calm Down! gesture if it is still missing.
Take Lady Tanith's invitation and enter Volcano Manor's service. Patches is loitering in the entrance corridor as a fellow Recusant.

lockouts.name: God-Devouring Serpent / Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy
lockouts.note: killing the lord of the manor first closes its assassination contracts and this whole branch with them

steps.text: Complete Tanith's first assassination contract, then speak to Patches again. He offloads his own target onto you with a Letter to Patches: kill Great Horned Tragoth.
Tragoth is waiting in the Magma Wyrm Makar arena in the Ruin-Strewn Precipice. Put him down.
Report back and exhaust Patches' dialogue, rest at a grace, then speak to him once more for the Magma Whip Candlestick.
After God-Devouring Serpent / Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy falls, return to Patches and exhaust his dialogue. He leaves the manor.
Find him injured in the corridor leading to Elemer of the Briar in the Shaded Castle. He hands you the Dancer's Castanets and asks you to pass them to Tanith.
Offer the castanets to Tanith, who is feasting on Rykard's remains in his arena. She turns them down and they leave your inventory regardless.

Go back to Murkwater Cave and open the chest one last time. He attacks out of habit; hold off and let him recognise you, and he grants the Patches' Crouch gesture and reopens his shop for the rest of the run.

missables.trigger: killing Patches at any point
missables.lost: every later stop, the Magma Whip Candlestick, the remaining gestures and his shop are gone. He is the single easiest NPC in the game to lose, because the game presents him as a boss.

missables.trigger: defeating God-Devouring Serpent / Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy before joining Volcano Manor
missables.lost: the Recusant branch, the Great Horned Tragoth contract and the Magma Whip Candlestick are all closed off.

missables.trigger: opening the Murkwater Cave chest and walking away without knocking him down to a surrender
missables.lost: he stays a hostile boss and none of the quest opens.

desc: Seluvis is the sneering sorcerer in the middle tower of the Three Sisters, nominally one of Ranni's retainers and privately a collector of people. He drugs the living into obedient dolls and keeps their bodies in a hidden cellar, and if you play along he will sell you those dolls as spirit summons. The line ends with him trying to use you to add Ranni herself to the shelf, which goes about as well as you would expect. Run it entirely before you hand Ranni the Fingerslayer Blade, because that single act kills him wherever he is standing.
whatItIs: Preceptor Seluvis is the sneering sorcerer in the middle tower of the Three Sisters, nominally one of Ranni's retainers and privately a collector of people he drugs into obedient dolls. He will sell those dolls as spirit summons if the character plays along, and the line ends with him trying to use the Tarnished to add Ranni herself to his shelf.
whyItMatters: The rewards include the Magic Scorpion Charm, Seluvis's Bell Bearing, the Preceptor's Set, and a choice of puppet summons (Nepheli Loux Puppet, Dung Eater Puppet, Dolores the Sleeping Arrow Puppet, Jarwight Puppet, or Finger Maiden Therolina Puppet). The potion is single-use so the Nepheli and Dung Eater puppets cannot both be obtained on the same character, and giving Ranni the Fingerslayer Blade kills Seluvis wherever he is standing, closing the entire line.
whenToUse: Kick off in Liurnia of the Lakes by entering Ranni's service at her tower in the Three Sisters and talking to his projection in the room. The potion decision happens at the Table of Lost Grace, the cellar discovery pulls you back up to his tower, and the Amber Starlight sits past the Altus Highway Junction. Close every one of those threads before Ranni ever sees the Fingerslayer Blade, since that hand-off is what kills him.
name: The puppeteer's scheme

steps.text: Enter Ranni's service at the top of her tower in the Three Sisters, then speak to the projections of Blaidd, Iji and Seluvis standing around the room before talking to Ranni again.
Walk down to the tower just south of hers and speak to the preceptor inside. Agree to his errand and he presses Seluvis's Potion into your hand, insisting it is a harmless gift.
Pick one of three ways to deal with the potion. Show it to Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing and he pours it away himself, then tells you to lie about it, which costs you nothing and harms nobody.

Or give it to Nepheli Loux, which needs the Omenkiller in the Village of the Albinaurics dead and Nepheli waiting in the hub's lower floor. She drops where she stands, and Pidia, Carian Servant later sells you what is left of her.
Or feed it to the Dung Eater, which needs him freed from his cell, beaten at the moat below the capital, and back in his gaol. He becomes the strongest of the puppets and Seluvis will stock him.
Whichever you chose, report back and exhaust him. His ordinary sorcery stock opens now.
Go to the ruins north-east of Ranni's tower and walk through the illusory floor. Take the stairs down into the cellar full of kneeling bodies and read the message that warns you not to touch them.
Confront him with the dialogue option about his chambers. Caught out, he offers to brew you puppets of your own in exchange for Starlight Shards. Buy at least one to move forward.
Speak to him again and pick the option about the scheme. He wants a rarer ingredient and will not say what it is for.

Fetch the Amber Starlight from the small grotto north-east of the Altus Highway Junction grace, past the long stair that a Tree Sentinel patrols, at the foot of the vast statue of Malenia and Miquella.
Hand the Amber Starlight over and he pays you the Magic Scorpion Charm on the spot.
Rest and reload, then collect the Amber Draught and the truth: it is meant for Ranni, and he expects you to be the one who serves it.

Ending A - offer Ranni the draught. She sees straight through it, freezes her own questline, and kills you outright if you speak to her three times afterwards. Only Absolution at the Church of Vows will restart her line.
Ending B - say nothing and simply continue Ranni's line. The moment she is given the Fingerslayer Blade the preceptor dies anyway, kneeling in his own tower like the dolls downstairs.
Either way, loot Seluvis's Bell Bearing and the Preceptor's Set from the body. The corpse still opens the puppet shop, so anything you did not buy is still available.

missables.trigger: completing step 14 (giving Ranni the Fingerslayer Blade)
missables.lost: everything above this line has to be finished first, because Seluvis dies at that moment and Pidia, Carian Servant dies with him.

missables.trigger: completing step 4 (giving Nepheli Loux the potion)
missables.lost: choosing the Dung Eater or Gideon instead means the Nepheli Loux Puppet cannot be obtained in this playthrough.

missables.trigger: completing step 5 (giving the Dung Eater the potion)
missables.lost: the potion is single-use, so the Dung Eater Puppet and the Nepheli Loux Puppet can never be collected on the same character, and feeding it to the Dung Eater ends his own questline early.

missables.trigger: completing step 13 (offering Ranni the Amber Draught)
missables.lost: Ranni's questline is frozen and can only be resumed by seeking Absolution at the Church of Vows.

desc: Ranni is a dead Empyrean piloting a doll, and hers is the longest and most rewarding questline in the base game. Following it drags you through three hidden underground regions most players never find, hands you the Dark Moon Greatsword, and unlocks the Age of the Stars ending. It is also the spine that Sorcerer Rogier's, Blaidd the Half-Wolf's, War Counselor Iji's and Preceptor Seluvis's quests all hang off, so the order you do it in decides how much of their content you ever see.
whatItIs: Ranni the Witch is a dead Empyrean piloting a doll who calls the character to serve her from a tower in Limgrave, setting off a chain that drags the story through three hidden underground regions and ends in a secret boss and the Age of the Stars ending. The spine of the questline also hangs Sorcerer Rogier's, Blaidd the Half-Wolf's, War Counselor Iji's, and Preceptor Seluvis's threads off it, so the order of play decides how much of their content is ever seen.
whyItMatters: The rewards include the Spirit Calling Bell, Lone Wolf Ashes, Carian Inverted Statue, Discarded Palace Key, Dark Moon Ring, Dark Moon Greatsword, and the Age of the Stars ending. Accepting her service after Starscourge Radahn is dead permanently skips the Blaidd the Half-Wolf and War Counselor Iji projections, handing the Fingerslayer Blade to her before Preceptor Seluvis's questline closes ends that line immediately, and holding the Dark Moon Ring while killing Astel, Naturalborn of the Void turns Blaidd hostile outside Ranni's Rise.
whenToUse: Begin in region-limgrave before Starscourge Radahn falls, and resolve Preceptor Seluvis's questline and Blaidd the Half-Wolf's questline before the Dark Moon Ring step at the Lake of Rot Shoreside. Do not accept the Frenzied Flame Proscription unless the Age of the Stars ending is no longer the goal, because that lock requires Miquella's Needle to reverse and would waste the summon at the Stone Platform.
name: Ranni's questline

steps.text: Optional, but the cheapest start. Once Melina has given you the Spectral Steed Whistle, ride Torrent at least once and rest at any grace, then go back to the Church of Elleh and speak to the small woman calling herself "Renna". Exhaust her lines for the Spirit Calling Bell and the Lone Wolf Ashes.
If you skipped Renna, buy the same two items from the Twin Maiden Husks instead - 1,000 runes for the bell, 200 for the ashes - so you can still summon spirits.
Clear Caria Manor and kill Royal Knight Loretta at the top of it. That opens the road north into the Three Sisters, the little valley holding Ranni's Rise.

Climb to the top floor of Ranni's Rise and talk to her. What she says here changes depending on whether you have already killed Starscourge Radahn or already handed Sorcerer Rogier the Black Knifeprint.

lockouts.name: Starscourge Radahn
lockouts.note: the Ranni's Rise projections of Blaidd the Half-Wolf and War Counselor Iji, and Blaidd's follow-up meeting at Siofra River Bank, are skipped and cannot be recovered

steps.text: Agree to serve her, walk back down the tower and speak to all three projections - War Counselor Iji, Blaidd the Half-Wolf and Preceptor Seluvis - then climb back up and talk to Ranni one more time. After that she sits asleep and will not answer you until you bring her something.
Kill Starscourge Radahn. His death pulls a star out of the sky, and the crater it leaves is the only way down into the buried city.
Work through Nokron to the chest north-east of the Night's Sacred Ground grace and take the Fingerslayer Blade out of it.
Carry the blade back to the sleeping Ranni. She wakes, accepts it, and gives you the Carian Inverted Statue - a key that Fia's questline needs and hers does not.

lockouts.name: Preceptor Seluvis's questline
lockouts.note: handing Ranni the Fingerslayer Blade ends Seluvis's questline the instant you do it

steps.text: Renna's Rise, the tower standing beside Ranni's, is unlocked now. Climb it and step into the sending gate at the top.
Pick up the Miniature Ranni doll lying near where the gate spits you out, rest at the Ainsel River Main grace, and pick "Talk to miniature Ranni" three separate times before she finally answers.
Optional flavour: she has extra lines if you rest at the Nokstella, Eternal City and Nokstella Waterfall Basin graces. Neither is needed to finish the quest.

Push past the Nokstella Waterfall Basin grace and kill the Baleful Shadow that invades wearing Blaidd's shape. It is an assassin sent by Ranni's own Two Fingers, not the real wolf. Ranni rewards the kill with the Discarded Palace Key.
Take that key up to Rennala's arena in the Academy of Raya Lucaria and open the chest there for the Dark Moon Ring.
Wade the rot lake, kill Astel, Naturalborn of the Void at the far end, and ride the lift beyond it. The lift will not move unless the Dark Moon Ring is already in your inventory.

lockouts.name: Blaidd the Half-Wolf's questline
lockouts.note: once you hold the ring and Astel is dead, Blaidd turns hostile outside Ranni's Rise and the only way past him is to kill him

steps.text: The lift comes up on the Moonlight Altar. Go to the Cathedral of Manus Celes and drop down the tunnel beside the altar to find Ranni sitting on the corpse of her Two Fingers. Touch her for the cutscene, then speak once more - she vanishes and leaves the Dark Moon Greatsword behind.
Beat the final boss, then find the blue summon sign on the Stone Platform in Leyndell, Ashen Capital and use it to call Ranni in. Choosing her here gives the Age of the Stars ending.

lockouts.name: the Frenzied Flame Proscription
lockouts.note: accepting the Frenzied Flame forces the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending on you instead, and only Miquella's Needle can undo it

missables.trigger: before defeating Starscourge Radahn
missables.lost: entering Ranni's service only after Radahn is dead skips the Ranni's Rise projections of Blaidd the Half-Wolf and War Counselor Iji, and Blaidd's Siofra River Bank meeting, permanently.

missables.trigger: before completing Preceptor Seluvis's questline
missables.lost: giving Ranni the Fingerslayer Blade ends Preceptor Seluvis's questline immediately.

missables.trigger: before completing Blaidd the Half-Wolf's questline
missables.lost: holding the Dark Moon Ring and defeating Astel, Naturalborn of the Void turns Blaidd hostile outside Ranni's Rise, ending his story there.

missables.trigger: before entering the Frenzied Flame Proscription
missables.lost: accepting the Frenzied Flame locks your ending to Lord of Frenzied Flame unless it is reversed with Miquella's Needle, which would waste the Age of the Stars summon.

desc: Freyja fought in Radahn's personal guard before the Scarlet Rot took her in the Swamp of Aeonia, and Miquella pulled the poison out of her wound with his own mouth. She follows him out of gratitude rather than fanaticism, so when the charm breaks she simply walks off to find out what her old general has to do with any of this. Her quest is short and it is bolted onto Sir Ansbach's: he can read the tablets she cannot, and the letter he writes her earns you the Golden Lion Shield, the highest guard boost of any medium shield in the game.
whatItIs: Redmane Freyja is a former knight of Radahn's personal guard, poisoned by the Scarlet Rot in the Swamp of Aeonia and healed by Miquella, who now follows him out of gratitude rather than faith. Her short quest in the Shadow Keep is tied to Sir Ansbach's, because he can read the tablets she cannot and the letter he writes her earns the Golden Lion Shield.
whyItMatters: Completing it grants Freyja's Greatsword and her full armour set, plus the Golden Lion Shield through Sir Ansbach's letter. The quest breaks if Shadow Keep is entered before her Gravesite Plain conversation, if the Secret Rite Scroll is never handed to Sir Ansbach, or if the Sealing Tree at Church of the Bud is burned before the letter is delivered, in which case she is found dead beside the Storehouse, Seventh Floor grace and only her set and greatsword can be recovered.
whenToUse: Available only through the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Begin at Three-Path Cross in the Gravesite Plain before stepping into Shadow Keep, and exhaust her dialogue there including the line about her helm. Complete the handover of the Secret Rite Scroll to Sir Ansbach at the Storehouse, First Floor and deliver the letter before the Sealing Tree behind the Church of the Bud is set alight.
name: Redmane Freyja's questline

steps.text: Follow the main road north of the Scorched Ruins to Three-Path Cross and speak to Freyja there. Exhaust everything, including the line about what she intends to look into, which is what sets her and Ansbach in motion.

lockouts.name: Shadow Keep
lockouts.note: her Gravesite Plain conversation

steps.text: Optional: her gold sign sits in front of the Divine Beast Dancing Lion's door inside Belurat, Tower Settlement, by the Stagefront grace. She is a strong ally for that fight.
With the Divine Beast dead, go back to Three-Path Cross and ask about the damage to her helm. She answers with her history as a Redmane knight.

lockouts.name: Shadow Keep
lockouts.note: the question about her helm

steps.text: Approach the black gates of the keep. Two lines of text announce a broken great rune and a broken charm, and Freyja decides to strike out on her own.
Optional: she and the Hornsent both leave gold signs outside the Golden Hippopotamus arena, just past the lift.

lockouts.name: Golden Hippopotamus
lockouts.note: her cooperator sign for that fight

steps.text: Work your way up the Specimen Storehouse to the Storehouse, Seventh Floor grace. Freyja is just past it, glaring at a wall of tablets she cannot read, and complaining that she should have asked Ansbach while she had the chance. Exhaust her.

lockouts.name: the Secret Rite Scroll handover to Sir Ansbach
lockouts.note: the letter is never written and the Golden Lion Shield is gone for the run

steps.text: Collect the Secret Rite Scroll from the small room below the Storehouse, Fourth Floor walkway, past the Fire Knight.
Go down to Ansbach in the library off the Storehouse, First Floor. Explain what Freyja has decided to do before you give him anything, then pass him the scroll.
Reload the area, speak to Ansbach again, and he gives you the Letter for Freyja.

Carry the letter back up to the seventh floor and pass it on. Freyja learns that Miquella means to bring Radahn's soul back and decides that endless war suits her general better than a clean death; she rewards you with the Golden Lion Shield. Talk again to finish her dialogue.

lockouts.name: the burning of the Sealing Tree at Church of the Bud
lockouts.note: she dies at this grace instead, leaving only her armour and greatsword

steps.text: Rest, then return to Ansbach once more and pass on Freyja's regards to close the exchange between them.
Freyja takes her place at Leda's shoulder for the ambush in the Cleansing Chamber Anteroom. Beat the group and her body carries Freyja's Greatsword and every piece of her armour.

missables.lost: her Gravesite Plain conversation, and with it the question about her helm.

missables.trigger: before defeating Golden Hippopotamus
missables.lost: her cooperator sign for that fight.

missables.trigger: before completing the Secret Rite Scroll handover to Sir Ansbach
missables.lost: the seventh-floor talk that unlocks the Letter for Freyja, and with it the Golden Lion Shield.

desc: Roderika starts the game as a broken young noblewoman waiting to die in a shack on the Stormhill road, and finishes it as the person who upgrades your summons. Getting her there is the single most practical NPC quest in the early game: without it nobody at Roundtable Hold will spend your Grave Glovewort, and every Spirit Ash you own stays stuck at +0. The chain is entirely conversation and one key item, so it costs almost no time. Do it before you clear Stormveil, because the first reward is gone the moment the story moves past Godrick.
whatItIs: Roderika, Spirit Tuner, starts the game as a broken noblewoman sitting in a shack on the Stormhill road waiting to die, and finishes as the person at Roundtable Hold who upgrades every Spirit Ash the character owns. Her chain is pure conversation plus one key item handoff, so it costs almost no time to complete.
whyItMatters: Without her at Roundtable Hold nobody will spend Grave Glovewort, and every Spirit Ash stays stuck at +0 for the rest of the run. The Sitting Sideways gesture is lost the moment Godrick the Grafted is defeated or Liurnia of the Lakes is entered, and killing Roderika means nobody else will tune Spirit Ashes, capping every summon at +0 permanently.
whenToUse: Start in region-limgrave at the Stormhill Shack before defeating Godrick the Grafted and before entering Liurnia of the Lakes. The Chrysalids' Memento in the courtyard room off the hall where the Grafted Scion waits must be collected and brought back to her at the shack before she relocates on her own.
name: Roderika's questline

steps.text: Roderika sits inside Stormhill Shack, on the path between Gatefront and the Stormveil bridge. Exhaust her dialogue to receive the Sitting Sideways gesture and the Spirit Jellyfish Ashes, your first real summon.

lockouts.name: Godrick the Grafted
lockouts.note: she relocates to Roundtable Hold and the Sitting Sideways gesture can never be obtained

steps.text: Inside Stormveil Castle, in the courtyard room off the hall where the Grafted Scion waits, take the Chrysalids' Memento from the corpse pile.
Bring the memento back to her at the shack and exhaust her dialogue. Reading it gives her a reason to leave, and she sets off for Roundtable Hold.

lockouts.name: Liurnia of the Lakes
lockouts.note: she leaves on her own, and the Golden Seed she would have handed you is left lying on the shack floor instead

steps.text: Find her by the fireplace in the central room and speak to her to collect the Golden Seed.
Walk down to Smithing Master Hewg at his anvil and pick "About Roderika". He notices she has a gift for spirit tuning.
Return to Roderika and tell her what the blacksmith said.
Go back to Hewg and run the chain "About Roderika", then "Would you watch over Roderika?", then "It's what she wants".
Reload the area. She is now sitting across from Hewg and will upgrade Spirit Ashes with Grave Glovewort and Ghost Glovewort.
Level any Spirit Ash to +4 or higher, then speak to her again for the Curtsy gesture.
Go back to the same corpse pile in Stormveil Castle. Now that she has stopped wearing her hood, the Crimson Hood is lying where the memento was. It is worth a permanent +1 Vigor.

After you burn the Erdtree at the Forge of the Giants, speak to Hewg and choose "Let's talk a while", then "Why are you still making weapons?". Speak to Roderika and choose "About Hewg", then return to Hewg for "What happened to her?".
After Beast Clergyman / Maliketh, the Black Blade falls, speak to Hewg with "About yourself" and then speak to Roderika for the last words of her story.

rewardNotes: Spirit Ash upgrades at Roundtable Hold

missables.trigger: defeating Godrick the Grafted
missables.lost: Roderika moves to Roundtable Hold on her own and the Sitting Sideways gesture is permanently lost.

missables.trigger: entering Liurnia of the Lakes and resting at a Site of Grace
missables.lost: the same relocation triggers, with the same loss; the Golden Seed is not lost, but it must be picked up off the shack floor rather than received from her.

missables.trigger: reaching Crumbling Farum Azula through the Forge of the Giants without ever starting the quest
missables.lost: the Chrysalids' Memento disappears from Stormveil Castle and is replaced by the Crimson Hood, so the memento handover can no longer be done.

missables.trigger: killing Roderika
missables.lost: nobody else in the game will tune Spirit Ashes, so every summon you own is capped at +0 for the rest of the run.

desc: Rya is the recruiter Volcano Manor sends out to find Tarnished worth turning into assassins, and helping her is the fastest way into the Manor questline without walking the whole length of Mt. Gelmir. Her own story is much darker than her manner suggests: she is not Tanith's daughter, she is not human, and the quest is about her finding that out. It ends with a choice you cannot take back, though every branch pays the same talisman. The whole thing dies the moment Rykard does, so do not rush the Manor.
whatItIs: Rya the Scout is the recruiter Volcano Manor sends out to find Tarnished worth turning into assassins, and her own story is about discovering she is not what she believes herself to be. Helping her is the fastest way into the Manor questline without walking the full length of Mt. Gelmir, and it ends with an irreversible choice at the Temple of Eiglay.
whyItMatters: The rewards are the Volcano Manor Invitation, Daedicar's Woe talisman, and Zorayas's Letter on the branch where neither killing nor drugging is chosen. The entire questline locks the moment Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy dies, so every uncompleted step is gone. The Tonic of Forgetfulness branch only exists if Tanith is asked for it before Rya is resolved at the Temple of Eiglay, and Tanith only offers it once Rya's true form has been seen.
whenToUse: Begin at the Laskyar Ruins in region-liurnia-of-the-lakes, buy Rya's Necklace from Blackguard Big Boggart at Boilprawn Shack, and work through the Manor contracts before going after Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy. The Tonic of Forgetfulness must be collected from Tanith at the Volcano Manor before the final decision at the Temple of Eiglay, and the Godskin Noble must be killed to find the Serpent's Amnion beyond it.
name: Rya's questline

steps.text: Find Rya standing in a small folly north of the Laskyar Ruins, out on the flooded plain. She is behind a barrier here and cannot be attacked. Exhaust her dialogue and she asks you to recover her stolen necklace.
Go to Boilprawn Shack, on the west side of the lake, and buy Rya's Necklace from Blackguard Big Boggart for 1,000 runes. Killing him drops it too, but that ends his own story.
Take the necklace back to Rya. She hands over the Volcano Manor Invitation, which is a straight teleport into the Manor.
Rya moves up to the Altus Plateau and waits either at the Lux Ruins or right beside the Altus Plateau end of the Grand Lift of Dectus. Speak to her and accept the ride to Volcano Manor.
Speak to Tanith inside the Manor and choose to join the Recusants. Rya now stands in the drawing room, and you are handed your first assassination contract.
Carry out the first contract and kill Old Knight Istvan, then collect your reward from Tanith. Talk to Rya in the drawing room afterwards.
Reload the area and open the room across the corridor from the drawing room, which was locked before. Rya is inside in her true serpent form. Exhaust everything she says.
Take the second contract, kill Rileigh the Idle, and take the reward from Tanith. Speak to Rya again in that same room.
Go into the room next door, push through the illusory wall at the back, and follow the passage down to the Prison Town Church grace. Rest there, then go back and speak to Rya once more.
Push on through the Manor and kill the Godskin Noble. The Serpent's Amnion is found beyond it - the caul Rya was born inside. Give it to her.
Optional but it unlocks the third ending: speak to Tanith and she gives you the Tonic of Forgetfulness, asking you to spare her daughter the truth.
Rya has moved to a small room above the Temple of Eiglay grace, past an Iron Virgin. She has learned what she is and asks you to kill her. This is where the quest branches.

lockouts.name: Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy
lockouts.note: the whole questline shuts down when Rykard dies, and any step you have not reached becomes unreachable

steps.text: Branch A - give her the Tonic of Forgetfulness. She falls asleep, and after you kill Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy she is back in the drawing room with no memory of any of it. Speak to her, reload, and Daedicar's Woe is waiting where she stood.
Branch B - do as she asks and kill her. Daedicar's Woe drops on the spot.

Branch C - refuse to kill her and never give her the tonic. After Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy is dead, return to the room above the Temple of Eiglay for Daedicar's Woe and Zorayas's Letter, where she explains she has gone to carry on Tanith's work herself.

missables.trigger: before defeating Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy
missables.lost: the entire questline locks the moment Rykard dies. Every step you have not yet completed is gone, including the invitation, the Serpent's Amnion conversation and Daedicar's Woe.

missables.trigger: before completing step 11
missables.lost: the Tonic of Forgetfulness branch only exists if you ask Tanith for the tonic before resolving Rya at the Temple of Eiglay, and Tanith only offers it once you have seen Rya's true form.

missables.trigger: before completing step 15
missables.lost: Zorayas's Letter only exists on the branch where you neither kill her nor drug her. The other two branches give the talisman without it.

missables.trigger: before completing step 2
missables.lost: killing Blackguard Big Boggart for the necklace instead of buying it ends his own questline.

desc: Gowry is the old man in the shack outside Sellia who trades favours for secrets. Run his first errand and he tells you how to unseal the sorcery town at his doorstep; run the rest and he opens a small sorcery stock, teaches you a rot incantation, and finally asks you to help murder the daughter he spent the whole quest saving. He is the engine behind Millicent's line rather than a separate story, so the two are followed side by side, but he pays out on his own: a shop, a spell, a talisman and a bell bearing.
whatItIs: Sage Gowry is the old man in a shack outside Sellia in Caelid who trades favours for secrets and serves as the engine behind Millicent's questline. His errands pay out a sorcery shop, a rot incantation, a talisman, and a bell bearing on their own, separate from whatever the Millicent branch resolves to.
whyItMatters: The rewards include Sellia's Secret, Pest Threads, the Flock's Canvas Talisman, and Gowry's Bell Bearing. His shop stays shut if the church is reloaded before returning to the shack after delivering the needle to Millicent, and Pest Threads is lost if Millicent's line reaches its end without the spell being purchased. The summon sign choice at the Prayer Room fixes his ending: only the branch where Millicent survives lets him be killed for the Flock's Canvas Talisman, while the other branch leaves him dead on the floor with the same two items to loot.
whenToUse: Start in region-caelid at Gowry's Shack near the Sellia Gateway, and run the first errand of killing Commander O'Neil at the Heart of Aeonia before moving on. The needle delivery to the Church of the Plague must be followed immediately by walking back down to the shack without reloading, or his shop never opens.
name: The sage of the rot

steps.text: Ride up to the Sellia Gateway at the town's southern entrance and step past it to the small shack beyond, then hear the old man out. Accept the bargain and he promises to explain how the sealed town below is opened.
Cross the scarlet swamp to its centre, where Commander O'Neil and his cleanrot spearmen hold the Heart of Aeonia. Kill him and the broken needle is yours.
Put the broken needle in the sage's hands. He pays immediately with Sellia's Secret, a scrap of paper explaining that lighting the three roof braziers over the town breaks its seal.
Rest anywhere, come back, and speak to him again to receive the repaired needle along with his second favour: take it to the woman dying in the church on the cliffs.

Deliver the needle in the Church of the Plague, then walk straight back down to the shack before you reload the church a second time. Doing it in that order opens his stock: Glintstone Stars, Night Shard and Night Maiden's Mist.

Once Millicent has been given the Valkyrie's Prosthesis on the Altus Plateau, return here. Pest Threads is now on the shelf for 7,500 runes, and buying it unlocks his account of Malenia and the Order of Rot.
After Millicent reaches Elphael, speak to him one more time. He drops the kindly-old-man act and asks you to side with her four sisters, because a betrayal by someone she trusts will make her bloom.
Settle the matter at the two summon signs above the rot pool below the Prayer Room grace. The sign you choose decides which version of step 9 you get.
If you fought at Millicent's side, he is still alive and grieving that she pulled the needle out. He can now be killed for good, and he leaves the Flock's Canvas Talisman and Gowry's Bell Bearing.
If you fought against her, the shack is already quiet: the sage is dead on the floor and the same two items are simply looted from him.

missables.trigger: completing step 5 (delivering the needle to Millicent)
missables.lost: reload the church before returning here and he steps out of the shack while Millicent occupies it, so his shop stays shut until she moves on.

missables.trigger: completing step 6 (buying Pest Threads)
missables.lost: reach the end of Millicent's line without buying the spell and its Malenia dialogue is gone; the spell itself has other sources.

missables.trigger: taking either summon sign at Elphael
missables.lost: his ending is fixed by that choice, and only the branch where Millicent survives the sisters lets you kill him yourself.

desc: Shabriri is the man who started the sickness of the Frenzied Flame, and by the time you meet him he has taken over the body of an NPC you probably already know. He is not a shopkeeper or an ally; he is a recruiter. His whole role is to point out that burning the Erdtree the intended way costs Melina her life, and to offer you a different job as Lord of Chaos instead. Taking that offer is one of the few genuinely irreversible decisions in the game, so read this page before you walk through a certain door under Leyndell.
whatItIs: Shabriri is the man who started the Frenzied Flame sickness, and by the time he appears at the Zamor Ruins in the Mountaintops of the Giants he is wearing the body of Bloody Finger Hunter Yura. He is not an ally or a shopkeeper; he is a recruiter who points out that burning the Erdtree the intended way costs Melina her life and offers a different ending in exchange.
whyItMatters: Accepting his path grants the Iron Kasa, Ronin's Armor, Ronin's Gauntlets, Ronin's Greaves, and the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending. Taking the Three Fingers embrace at the Frenzied Flame Proscription ends Melina's accord permanently and closes every other ending until Miquella's Needle is used in Dragonlord Placidusax's arena. Entering the Mountaintops of the Giants while Bloody Finger Hunter Yura's questline is unfinished kills that line wherever it stood, whether or not it had been started.
whenToUse: The Zamor Ruins grace is reached by riding the Grand Lift of Rold up into the Mountaintops of the Giants. Do not enter that region until Bloody Finger Hunter Yura's questline is resolved, and exhaust every line of dialogue at the Zamor Ruins before the Frenzied Flame Proscription door is touched, because that door is the last point where the character can still walk away.
name: Shabriri and the Frenzied Flame

steps.text: Ride up the Grand Lift of Rold and stop at the Zamor Ruins grace near the start of the region; a blindfolded swordsman is waiting there.
Look at him properly before you talk. He is wearing the body of Bloody Finger Hunter Yura, and he says so outright, which is the game's way of telling you Yura's own story has already ended.
Exhaust every line he has. He explains what Melina intends to do at the forge, that your ascent needs her as kindling, and that you could burn instead of her.
Rest at a grace afterwards. Melina now has a new conversation in which she asks you plainly not to meddle with the Frenzied Flame, which is the only warning you get.
If you want the other road, kill Morgott, the Omen King and then drop into the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds beneath the capital, following it through to the Cathedral of the Forsaken.
Take the long ladder down to the Frenzied Flame Proscription grace at the very bottom of that dungeon.
Unequip every piece of armour from all four slots. The sealed door will not open for a clothed Tarnished, and this is the last point at which you can still walk away.

Interact with the door. The Three Fingers embrace you, the cutscene plays, and you come out carrying the Frenzied Flame with your eyes burning; if Lightseeker Hyetta's own story has reached its end down here, touching her now is what yields the Frenzied Flame Seal.
Go back to the Zamor Ruins. Shabriri is gone, his work done, and his Ronin's armour is left on the ground by the grace for you to take.

Rest at the Forge of the Giants and pick "Listen to the flames" instead of Melina's old option, which pushes the story on to Crumbling Farum Azula with the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending now locked in.
Optional. Much later, in the ash-covered capital, Shabriri leaves a cooperator sign outside Godfrey, First Elden Lord; he fights with the same frenzy incantations he used to preach at you.

The way out, if you change your mind. Finish Millicent's questline and kill Malenia, Blade of Miquella to obtain Miquella's Needle, then use it inside Dragonlord Placidusax's arena to burn the Frenzied Flame out and reopen the other endings.

missables.trigger: completing the Three Fingers embrace at Frenzied Flame Proscription
missables.lost: Melina ends her accord and leaves permanently, and every ending except Lord of Frenzied Flame closes until Miquella's Needle is used in Dragonlord Placidusax's arena.

missables.trigger: completing the Three Fingers embrace at Frenzied Flame Proscription before talking to Shabriri

desc: Ansbach is the old commander of Mohg's Pureblood Knights, and the only follower of Miquella who treats the whole pilgrimage as an investigation rather than an act of faith. He asks you to report every one of Miquella's crosses you find, and once the charm on the followers breaks he goes into the Shadow Keep looking for what happened to his lord's corpse. This is the single most valuable questline in the expansion: finish it and Ansbach fights beside you both against Leda's ambush and against the final boss, which is the difference between a brutal solo fight and a manageable one. It also feeds Redmane Freyja's quest, so run the two together.
whatItIs: Sir Ansbach is the old commander of Mohg's Pureblood Knights who treats Miquella's pilgrimage as an investigation rather than an act of faith, and he asks the character to report every cross of Miquella found along the road. Once the charm on the followers breaks he goes into the Shadow Keep looking for what happened to his lord's corpse, and his gold summon signs fight beside the character in two of the hardest encounters in the expansion.
whyItMatters: The completed chain hands over Ansbach's Longbow, the Obsidian Lamina, the Furious Blade of Ansbach, his full attire set, and the Letter for Freyja that plugs into Redmane Freyja's thread. Take Needle Knight Leda's side at the Storehouse signs and you lose the Obsidian Lamina, the Furious Blade of Ansbach, and both of his gold summons in Enir-Ilim, and the entire line collapses if the Secret Rite Scroll is still undelivered when the Church of the Bud kindling happens.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is a prerequisite for this thread. Start at Main Gate Cross in the Gravesite Plain, work the cross-reporting steps across the Cerulean Coast and Scadu Altus, and finish the Secret Rite Scroll handover before Messmer's Kindling is used at the Church of the Bud. Take the gold summon sign at the Storehouse, First Floor rather than the red one, or the quest ends and both later summons are lost.
name: Sir Ansbach's questline

steps.text: Talk to Ansbach beside Main Gate Cross, at the foot of the road up to Belurat, Tower Settlement. Head west from Three-Path Cross to reach him. He asks you to tell him about any of Miquella's crosses you come across.

Optional: ride south from the Cerulean Coast grace to the cross standing on the coastal cliff, touch it, then go back and pick "Speak of the cross at the coast". He works out that Miquella shed St. Trina here.
Optional: unseal the spiritspring north of the Fort of Reprimand, ride up to the cross on the cliff above it, then report it with "Speak of the cross where the eye was abandoned".

Ride north from Highroad Cross until the Shadow Keep gates loom and the screen reports a great rune shattered. That single event pushes every follower of Miquella forward at once, so clear your outstanding conversations first.
Return to Main Gate Cross, exhaust his new dialogue, then reload the area. Ansbach leaves for the Shadow Keep.
Find him again in the room north of the Storehouse, First Floor grace. Go past the ghost casting fire and take the doorway on the right before the stairs.

Fetch the Secret Rite Scroll. From Storehouse, Fourth Floor go outside and left along the walkway, up past the Fire Knight, then down the staircase on the left before the giant bats; the scroll is on a desk in the room at the bottom.
Climb to Storehouse, Seventh Floor and exhaust Freyja, who is struggling to read the tablets there. Do this while the scroll is still in your pocket.

lockouts.name: the Secret Rite Scroll handover to Sir Ansbach
lockouts.note: Ansbach leaves after the handover and the Letter for Freyja is never written, which also kills the Golden Lion Shield

steps.text: Back at Ansbach: tell him about Freyja's decision first, then hand over the Secret Rite Scroll. He reads it and concludes that Miquella means to raise Radahn's soul in Mohg's body.
Reload the area, speak to him again for the Letter for Freyja, carry it up to Freyja for the Golden Lion Shield, then come back and pass on what she said.
Exhaust Leda at Highroad Cross until she names Ansbach as her next target. Her thread has to move before his can.
Two summon signs appear where Ansbach was sitting. Take the GOLD sign to fight beside him; the red sign kills him, ends his quest and costs you both of his later summons.

lockouts.name: the burning of the Sealing Tree at Church of the Bud
lockouts.note: the two summon signs, and with them any say in whether he lives

steps.text: Beat Messmer and Romina, then burn the Sealing Tree behind the Church of the Bud with Messmer's Kindling to open Enir-Ilim.
At the Cleansing Chamber Anteroom, touch Ansbach's gold sign (and Thiollier's, if you have it) BEFORE you touch Leda's red sign, then win the brawl.
Ride the lift up and find him standing on the stairs before the Divine Gate. Exhaust him and admit that you were the one who killed Mohg; he takes it as an honourable death.

lockouts.name: Promised Consort Radahn
lockouts.note: his last conversation

steps.text: His gold sign sits outside the final arena. Summon him or not, the sign existing is what matters: after Promised Consort Radahn falls, his body by the arena entrance carries Obsidian Lamina, his full set and the Furious Blade of Ansbach.

missables.lost: the seventh-floor talk with Freyja, and with it the Letter for Freyja and the Golden Lion Shield.

missables.trigger: siding with Needle Knight Leda at the Storehouse, First Floor signs
missables.lost: Obsidian Lamina, the Furious Blade of Ansbach and both of his gold summon signs in Enir-Ilim. You get his armour set and the Retaliatory Crossed-Tree instead.

missables.trigger: siding with Sir Ansbach at the Storehouse, First Floor signs
missables.lost: the Retaliatory Crossed-Tree, which only Leda hands out.

missables.trigger: helping the Hornsent against Leda earlier

missables.lost: his last conversation on the Divine Gate stairs.

desc: Gideon runs Roundtable Hold, hoards everything anyone knows about the demigods, and wants the throne himself. He is a walking information desk for the first half of the game and a trading post for the second: tell him what you find about the four demigods he cannot locate and he pays in late-game spells. His questline also triggers the Ensha ambush in the Hold, and it closes with Gideon standing in the burned capital as a boss.
whatItIs: Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing, runs Roundtable Hold and hoards everything anyone knows about the demigods, and he wants the throne himself. He functions as a walking information desk for the first half of the game and a trading post for the second: report what is found about the four demigods he cannot locate and he pays in late-game spells and gear, and the questline closes with him standing in the burned capital as a boss.
whyItMatters: The rewards span Black Flame's Protection, Lord's Divine Fortification, Fevor's Cookbook [3], Law of Causality, the Scepter of the All-Knowing, and his full armour set. Every dialogue reward is lost the moment Maliketh, the Black Blade is defeated, though the four spell items reappear at the Twin Maiden Husks once the Rune of Death is unsealed. Handing him Seluvis's Potion destroys it permanently and removes both the Nepheli Loux Puppet and the Dung Eater Puppet from the run.
whenToUse: The first conversation happens in region-roundtable-hold after killing any shardbearer and speaking with Finger Reader Enia. The later intel steps require lighting graces in Leyndell, Consecrated Snowfield, and Mohgwyn Palace, and the final boss fight in the Erdtree Sanctuary comes after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade. Ensha of the Royal Remains must be killed before asking Gideon about the secret medallions, or those lines are gone with him.
name: Gideon Ofnir's questline

steps.text: On your first trip to the Hold, find him in the central chamber near the table and exhaust his dialogue; he calls you a mere visitor and then moves into his study.

Kill any shardbearer, speak with Finger Reader Enia, then go back to Gideon; he welcomes you as a full member and opens intel on Godrick the Grafted, Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, Starscourge Radahn, Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy and Morgott, the Omen King.
Once you have met Nepheli Loux, ask him about her; he admits he raised her, used her, and dropped her when she started asking questions about the Village of the Albinaurics.
Optional. Hand him Seluvis's Potion so he can destroy it, but think first, because the potion is the only way to obtain either puppet it could have made.
Pick up either half of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, then fast travel back to the Hold; Ensha of the Royal Remains invades in the northern corridor. Kill him.
With Ensha dead, ask Gideon "About Ensha" and then "About the secret medallions"; he apologises for his man and tells you where the other half is hidden.

lockouts.name: Maliketh, the Black Blade
lockouts.note: Gideon turns hostile and stops talking for good

steps.text: Rest at any grace inside the capital so his subject changes; he now wants word of Ranni the Witch, Mohg, Lord of Blood, Malenia, Blade of Miquella and Miquella himself, and starts paying for it.
Light any Site of Grace inside Miquella's Haligtree, return to the Hold and pick "About the secret medallions" to be paid with Black Flame's Protection.

lockouts.name: Maliketh, the Black Blade
lockouts.note: the spell must be bought from the Twin Maiden Husks instead

steps.text: Kill Malenia, Blade of Miquella, report back and pick "About the Haligtree roots" for Lord's Divine Fortification.

lockouts.name: Maliketh, the Black Blade
lockouts.note: the spell must be bought from the Twin Maiden Husks instead

steps.text: Light a Site of Grace inside Mohgwyn Palace, report back and pick "Mohgwyn Palace" for Fevor's Cookbook [3].

lockouts.name: Maliketh, the Black Blade
lockouts.note: the cookbook must be bought from the Twin Maiden Husks instead

steps.text: Kill Mohg, Lord of Blood, go back and pick "About the Lord of Blood's cocoon"; Gideon calls it one of the last pieces he needed and pays with Law of Causality.

lockouts.name: Maliketh, the Black Blade
lockouts.note: the spell must be bought from the Twin Maiden Husks instead

steps.text: Kill Maliketh, the Black Blade to unseal the Rune of Death and turn the capital to ash; Gideon is now waiting in the Erdtree Sanctuary and every conversation option is gone.

Beat him. He only has seven memory slots, so his spell list swaps rather than grows: killing Rykard, Malenia or Mohg first hands him their signature spell and pushes one of his defaults out. He drops the Scepter of the All-Knowing and the All-Knowing set.

desc: Rogier is the well-mannered sorcerer who explains what is actually going on in the opening third of the game - the Night of Black Knives, Those Who Live in Death, and who murdered Godwyn. He is also a genuinely good early shop, selling three ashes of war and handing you a fully upgraded rapier. His quest is a chain of Roundtable Hold conversations that ends with him dying of Deathroot, and it is the door into Ranni's questline, so most players run the two together.
whatItIs: Sorcerer Rogier is a well-mannered scholar who explains the Night of Black Knives, Those Who Live in Death, and who murdered Godwyn, and he also runs a genuinely useful early shop selling three ashes of war and a fully upgraded rapier. His quest is a chain of Roundtable Hold conversations that ends with him dying of Deathroot, and it is the doorway into Ranni's questline so most players run the two together.
whyItMatters: The rewards are Rogier's Rapier, Rogier's Letter, Rogier's Bell Bearing, and three Ashes of War: Glintstone Pebble, Carian Greatsword, and Spinning Weapon. Seeing his bloodstain by the malformed corpse under Stormveil Castle before Godrick the Grafted is dead removes him from the castle permanently. Skipping the "About D" dialogue means Rogier's Letter never appears, and his shop closes the moment he becomes unresponsive with no second chance to buy the ashes of war.
whenToUse: The optional first meeting is in the chapel past the Rampart Tower grace inside Stormveil Castle in region-limgrave. The main chain runs through Roundtable Hold and requires a trip to Black Knife Catacombs on the eastern shore of Liurnia, then a visit to Ranni's Rise in the Three Sisters to agree to serve her. Buy everything from him and exhaust all dialogue before the final reload, because his shop is gone once he slumps at the table.
name: Rogier's questline

steps.text: Optional but worth it: find Rogier kneeling in the chapel just past the Rampart Tower grace inside Stormveil Castle. Exhaust his dialogue - he warns you about Godrick's Tarnished hunters and offers to teach his combat sorceries.
Deep in the lower reaches of Stormveil, past the Ulcerated Tree Spirit, is a malformed corpse with Rogier's bloodstain beside it. Do not go looking for it yet.

lockouts.name: Godrick the Grafted
lockouts.note: finding that bloodstain first makes Rogier disappear from Stormveil for good, taking his castle dialogue with him

steps.text: Once Godrick is dead, Rogier turns up in Roundtable Hold. Tell him you beat Godrick, then ask about the corpse below Stormveil. He gives you Rogier's Rapier at +8 and opens his shop.
Before you go anywhere, pick the "About D" dialogue option and hear it out. Nothing marks this as important and it is the single easiest thing to lose in his whole quest.

lockouts.name: step 14
lockouts.note: if you never hear the "About D" line, Rogier's Letter never appears on his corpse and you lose the pointer to D's brother

steps.text: Talk to Fia in the side room and let her explain the Black Knifeprints the assassins left behind.
Go down into Black Knife Catacombs, on the eastern shore of Liurnia, and kill the Black Knife Assassin at the end of it. It drops the Black Knifeprint.
Hand Rogier the Black Knifeprint. Optionally ask Fia about him afterwards for extra dialogue.
Rest and reload, then speak to him again. He has read the enchantment on the print and names Ranni the Witch as the one who armed the assassins, and asks you to go look at her.
Ride up to Ranni's Rise in the Three Sisters and talk to Ranni. She is dismissive and sends you away, which is the point.
Go back and tell Rogier what happened. He asks you to go further and actually enter her service.
Return to Ranni's Rise and this time agree to become one of her vassals. This is the same step that starts Ranni's own questline.
Report back to Rogier. You can now ask why he wants the cursemark, and he admits he is trying to save Those Who Live in Death. He also tells you the Deathroot is winning.
Buy everything you want from him now and empty out every remaining dialogue option.

lockouts.name: step 14
lockouts.note: once he stops responding his shop closes and every line you have not already heard is gone

steps.text: Reload the area and Rogier is slumped and unresponsive. Reload once more and he is dead, leaving his gear, Rogier's Bell Bearing and Rogier's Letter behind.
Optional epilogue: if you follow Fia's questline to the Prince of Death's Throne, she raises Rogier as one of her champions and you have to fight him there.

missables.trigger: before completing step 14

missables.trigger: before completing step 14

desc: Thops is a talentless student who was standing outside the Academy of Raya Lucaria on the day it sealed its gates, and he has been sitting in a ruined church ever since, trying to find a way back in. His quest is short, entirely contained in Liurnia, and it hands out the Erudition gesture - which you need to open the Converted Fringe Tower and the Converted Tower - plus a spell and an ash of war that share a name. The whole thing hinges on one easy-to-miss detail: there are two Academy Glintstone Keys, and he will only take the second one.
whatItIs: Sorcerer Thops is a talentless student stranded outside the Academy of Raya Lucaria who sits in a ruined church on the cliff road out of Stormveil Castle, trying to find a way back inside. His short quest in Liurnia hinges on one easy-to-miss detail: there are two Academy Glintstone Keys and he will only accept the second one.
whyItMatters: The rewards include the Erudition gesture, Thops's Barrier spell, Ash of War: Thops's Barrier, the Academy Glintstone Staff, Thops's Bell Bearing, and access to Gavel of Haima and Cannon of Haima in the Converted Fringe Tower. Without the Erudition gesture the Converted Fringe Tower puzzle cannot be solved at all, putting those two items permanently out of reach. The Ash-of-War Scarab at the Church of Irith only spawns after Thops leaves for the Academy, so the ash of war cannot be collected before the quest is finished.
whenToUse: Start at the Church of Irith in region-liurnia-of-the-lakes, the cliff road reached right after leaving Stormveil Castle. The first Academy Glintstone Key is taken from the corpse near Glintstone Dragon Smarag in north-western Liurnia and used personally to enter the Academy, while the second key is looted from the rafters above the Church of the Cuckoo inside. Bring that second key back to the Church of Irith before doing anything else in the Academy.
name: Thops's questline

steps.text: Find Thops sitting in the Church of Irith, on the cliff road you come out on after leaving Stormveil Castle. Speak to him and agree to donate 10 runes, which is what opens his shop.

Buy what you want from him now - Glintstone Pebble for 1,000 runes, Glintstone Arc for 1,500 and Starlight for 2,500. He is the only sorcery instructor in the game who cannot be given scrolls, so this list never grows.
Get the FIRST Academy Glintstone Key from the corpse on the little island guarded by Glintstone Dragon Smarag, in north-western Liurnia. Use this one yourself to pass the seal at the Academy gate.
Inside the Academy, climb onto the rafters above the Church of the Cuckoo and take the SECOND Academy Glintstone Key from the body up there. This is the one Thops will accept.
Carry that second key back to the Church of Irith and hand it to Thops. He gives you the Erudition gesture and sets off for the Academy at last.

Go back into the Academy. Thops's body is slumped at a desk just outside the room holding the Schoolhouse Classroom grace - he got in, sat down and died. Loot him for Thops's Barrier, an Academy Glintstone Staff and Thops's Bell Bearing.
Return one last time to the Church of Irith. An Ash-of-War Scarab now spawns there; kill it for Ash of War: Thops's Barrier, the weapon-skill version of his spell.

Take Erudition to the Converted Fringe Tower and perform it in front of the imp statue seal to open it - Gavel of Haima and Cannon of Haima are inside. The same gesture also solves the Converted Tower, although that one's reward can be reached by climbing the outside walls instead.

missables.lost: Thops will refuse the Academy Glintstone Key found near Glintstone Dragon Smarag, because that copy is reserved for opening the Academy gate. You must bring him the second key from the rafters above the Church of the Cuckoo.

missables.trigger: before completing step 5
missables.lost: the Ash-of-War Scarab at the Church of Irith only spawns after Thops leaves for the Academy, so Ash of War: Thops's Barrier cannot be collected until you have finished his quest.

missables.trigger: before completing step 8
missables.lost: without the Erudition gesture the Converted Fringe Tower puzzle cannot be solved at all, which puts Gavel of Haima and Cannon of Haima permanently out of reach.

desc: Sellen is the exiled sorceress who takes you on as an apprentice in a cellar in Limgrave, and she is the reason most sorcery builds get off the ground at all - her shop is the first real spell selection in the game. Her quest asks you to hunt down her two banished masters, Azur and Lusat, for the two strongest sorceries in the game, then to carry her soul across the map and put it in a new body. It ends in a co-op duel at the Academy and a genuinely bleak twist. It is long and it crosses half the world map, so start it early.
whatItIs: Sorceress Sellen is an exiled sorceress who takes the character on as an apprentice in a cellar in Limgrave, and her shop is the first real spell selection available in the game. Her quest asks for the hunting of her two banished masters, Azur and Lusat, for their sorceries, then for carrying her soul across the map into a new body, and it ends in a co-op duel at the Academy with a genuinely bleak twist.
whyItMatters: The rewards include the Nod In Thought gesture, Sellian Sealbreaker, Comet Azur, Stars of Ruin, Starlight Shards, Glintstone Kris, Eccentric's Set, and the Witch's Glintstone Crown. The conversation about Seluvis's Introduction and the Radahn Festival only exists while Starscourge Radahn is still alive, and Castellan Jerren never appears at Witchbane Ruins unless he was spoken to at Redmane Castle after that fight. Taking the red summon sign outside the Raya Lucaria Grand Library instead of the gold one ends the questline and forfeits the Eccentric's Set, Glintstone Kris, and Witch's Glintstone Crown.
whenToUse: Begin at the Waypoint Ruins Cellar in Limgrave after defeating the Mad Pumpkin Head, then work through Mt. Gelmir and Sellia Hideaway in Caelid before Starscourge Radahn falls, because that battle removes her hidden protection. Hold the dialogue line about Lusat's location until the co-op duel at the Raya Lucaria Grand Library is won, since speaking it after she reaches the Academy turns her into a Graven Mass on the next reload.
name: Sellen's questline

steps.text: Clear the Waypoint Ruins east of the Church of Elleh, kill the Mad Pumpkin Head in the cellar, and talk to Sellen behind him. Pick "I wish to learn glintstone sorceries" to become her apprentice - that gives the Nod In Thought gesture and opens her shop.

Optional: if you are carrying Seluvis's Introduction and the Radahn Festival has not started yet, she has an extra conversation about it. You get that letter by progressing Blaidd the Half-Wolf's questline and asking Preceptor Seluvis about Nokron.

lockouts.name: Starscourge Radahn
lockouts.note: once the Radahn Festival is over this conversation is gone

steps.text: Climb Mt. Gelmir, go past the Hermit Village to the cliff edge, and touch the near-petrified Primeval Sorcerer Azur to learn Comet Azur.

Back at the Waypoint Ruins, pick "Show Azur's Sorcery", then "Tell me your story", then "Let us journey together", and finally "I have a favor to ask" to receive the Sellian Sealbreaker. The options only appear in that order.

Take the Sealbreaker to Sellia Hideaway in eastern Caelid, work through the illusory-wall cave to the sealed tunnel at the back, and use it to reach Primeval Sorcerer Lusat. Touching him teaches Stars of Ruin.

You can now pick "Lusat's location" when you talk to Sellen, which pays out Starlight Shards. You may also save this line for later - it is the trigger that ends her story, so hold it if you want her alive longer.

Go to Redmane Castle and speak to Castellan Jerren before the Radahn Festival, then again after you have beaten Starscourge Radahn. If you never talk to him he will not show up later at Witchbane Ruins.
Defeat Starscourge Radahn. The stars move, and Sellen loses the immortality that was keeping her hidden.
Talk to Sellen again. She admits the woman you have been speaking to is only a projection and tells you her real body is chained up in the far south.

Ride down to Witchbane Ruins on the Weeping Peninsula - just below the Church of Marika, past the plain of the Wandering Mausoleum - and drop into the cellar. Speak to the shackled Sellen and accept her Primal Glintstone.
Reload the area and go back down. Castellan Jerren is standing over the empty body - he only appears if you spoke to him at Redmane Castle after Radahn died.
Go to the Three Sisters and find the ruined structure north-east of Ranni's Rise. Roll into or hit the ground to reveal a hidden staircase down into Preceptor Seluvis's puppet cellar.

Walk through the illusory wall at the far end of the puppet room to find a doll that looks exactly like Sellen's old body. Interact with it to insert Sellen's Primal Glintstone and put her back together.
Beat Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon if you have not already. Two summon signs now sit outside the Grand Library door, one red and one gold.

Use the GOLD sign to be summoned as Sellen's cooperator against Witch-Hunter Jerren; the red one is the opposite side of the same duel and does not progress her questline. Beating Jerren pays out the Eccentric's Set.

lockouts.name: step 16
lockouts.note: only the gold sign carries her questline forward, and everything after this point is lost if she dies here

steps.text: Sellen has taken Rennala's place in the arena. Speak to her for the Glintstone Kris, and hand over any remaining scrolls or academy business now.
Tell her "Lusat's location" (if you saved it from step 6) and take the Starlight Shards.
Reload the area. Sellen has become a Graven Mass slumped against the side of the room. Take the Witch's Glintstone Crown from her. Her shop and scroll-turn-ins still work even in this state.
Optional cleanup: with Sellen installed at the Academy you can return to Azur on Mt. Gelmir and Lusat in Sellia Hideaway to loot their armour sets.

missables.lost: Sellen's conversation about Seluvis's Introduction and the Radahn Festival only exists while the festival is still ahead of you.

missables.trigger: before completing step 11
missables.lost: Castellan Jerren never appears at Witchbane Ruins unless you spoke to him at Redmane Castle after defeating Starscourge Radahn.

missables.trigger: before completing step 16
missables.lost: taking the red summon sign outside the Raya Lucaria Grand Library instead of the gold one ends Sellen's questline and forfeits the Eccentric's Set, the Glintstone Kris and the Witch's Glintstone Crown.

missables.trigger: before completing step 18
missables.lost: telling Sellen "Lusat's location" after she reaches the Academy is what turns her into a Graven Mass on the next reload, so hear anything else you want from her first.

desc: St. Trina sleeps at the bottom of a flooded ravine south of the Cerulean Coast, cradled in a purple flower, and she is the part of Miquella he threw away on his climb toward godhood. Her questline is really a conversation: you drink her nectar until she is willing to speak, then carry what she says back to Thiollier, the masked poisoner who has spent his life chasing the one night of sleep she gave him. Every sip puts you down for good and sends you back to the grace, so the whole thing runs on patience, and the payoff is a sleep talisman plus Thiollier's needle and robes at the very end of the expansion. It is also the one thread in the DLC where a character states outright what she wants done about Miquella.
whatItIs: St. Trina is the discarded half of Miquella, asleep inside a purple flower at the bottom of a flooded ravine below the Cerulean Coast. Her questline is a conversation run through repeated deaths: drink her nectar until she speaks, then carry her words back to Thiollier, the masked poisoner who still wants the sleep she once gave him.
whyItMatters: Completing the thread yields St. Trina's Smile, Thiollier's Hidden Needle, and his full robe set after Promised Consort Radahn falls. Stepping into Shadow Keep closes the syrup errand and costs you the Dragon Communion Priestess's spirit ash, and reaching Enir-Ilim moves every follower to the tower so the garden conversations stall permanently.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion gates this one. Kill the Putrescent Knight in the flowered garden arena, then work through the nectar sips and Thiollier's dialogue before stepping into Shadow Keep or Enir-Ilim.
name: St. Trina's questline

steps.text: Find Thiollier sitting alone at the crossroads grace on the north-east edge of the plain, well away from the rest of Miquella's followers, and exhaust his dialogue.
Ride west to the crossroads grace outside Belurat and keep talking to Moore, the hulking scavenger-merchant camped there, until he entrusts you with a bottle of black syrup.

lockouts.name: Shadow Keep
lockouts.note: the syrup errand closes and you also forfeit the spirit ash the Dragon Communion Priestess would have left you

steps.text: Bring the syrup back to Thiollier. He mixes it into his own concoction, hands you one and adds it to his stock.

lockouts.name: Shadow Keep
lockouts.note: the syrup errand closes and you also forfeit the spirit ash the Dragon Communion Priestess would have left you

steps.text: Ride to the southernmost tip of the pale coast, where the ground opens into a chasm. Face the pit and take the stairway cut into its right-hand side down into the ravine.
Descend the whole ravine, past the water-filled coffins and the tumbling putrescence, until you reach the arena at the very bottom.
Kill the Putrescent Knight. A grace lights in the corner of the arena, and the flowered garden behind it holds the sleeping saint.
Approach St. Trina. She will not speak yet; imbibing her nectar simply puts you to sleep for good and returns you to the grace.
Go back to Thiollier and tell him where she is. He will also set off on his own if you kill the Golden Hippopotamus, step into the Church District, or find the grace deep in the ravine.

lockouts.name: Enir-Ilim
lockouts.note: Miquella's followers all move to the tower and the garden conversations can no longer be finished

steps.text: Return to the garden. Thiollier is now kneeling past the grace; exhaust his lines, rest to reload the area, then exhaust them again.

Drink from the flower, reloading at the grace after each sip. Six sips in total earn three separate lines: that Miquella must be stopped, that godhood would only cage him, and finally that you must kill him and forgive him.
Repeat her words to Thiollier. He calls you a liar the first time, so keep speaking to him and offer them again until he stops arguing.
Rest at the grace. Thiollier immediately invades you in a black fury; beating him drops the St. Trina's Smile talisman and leaves him kneeling in the garden again.
Talk to the beaten Thiollier one more time and finish passing on what the saint told you. If the option refuses to appear, you have not yet heard all three of her lines.
His gold summon sign now sits outside both of the tower's final fights. He is a genuinely useful ally against Promised Consort Radahn, but the reward does not depend on summoning him.
After Promised Consort Radahn falls, reload the area and search the boss room. Thiollier's body lies there with his hidden needle and all four pieces of his robes.

desc: Tanith is the hostess of Volcano Manor and the consort of the serpent demigod who lives beneath it. She offers you a job: kill Tarnished who still serve the Erdtree, one contract at a time, and she pays in a spell, a katana and a talisman. The whole thing is a slow-burning side story that runs from Limgrave to the Mountaintops before it finally opens the shortcut to Rykard himself, and the single most important thing to understand is that killing Rykard ends it instantly, no matter how far along you are.
whatItIs: Tanith, Volcano Manor Proprietress, is the hostess of Volcano Manor on Mt. Gelmir and the consort of the serpent demigod who lives beneath it. She offers a job: kill Tarnished who still serve the Erdtree, one contract at a time, paying in a spell, a katana, and a talisman, and the whole thing is a slow-burning side story that runs from Limgrave to the Mountaintops before opening the shortcut to Rykard.
whyItMatters: The payoff spans Magma Shot, the Serpentbone Blade, Taker's Cameo, the full Consort's set, Aspects of the Crucible: Breath, the Blasphemous Blade, Rykard's Rancor, and the Tonic of Forgetfulness. Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy must be saved for last because every unfinished contract closes the instant he falls. If Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood falls before Rya's serpent reveal is reached, Tanith's conversation about her daughter is lost and the Tonic of Forgetfulness can only be retrieved from her empty chair.
whenToUse: The Abductor in Limgrave can carry a fresh character into Volcano Manor from the earliest stretches of the game, while riding over Mt. Gelmir or using Rya's teleport from the Altus Plateau are the later routes in. Finish every contract and grab the Serpent-Hunter from the corpse pile at the arena entrance before touching the fog, since killing Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy seals every remaining step of the line for good.
name: Volcano Manor and Lord Rykard

steps.text: Get into the manor. You can ride the long way over Mt. Gelmir, let Rya teleport you there once you reach the Altus Plateau, or take the cheap route and let the Abductor Virgin under the Academy of Raya Lucaria drag you off.
Speak to Tanith just right of the entrance grace and choose to join the family; she gives you the Drawing-Room Key, which is also the only key to the rest of the manor.

lockouts.name: Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy
lockouts.note: the whole questline closes

steps.text: Take the corridor to her right and open the first door on the left. Pick up the letter naming your first target from the table, and the Recusant Finger beside it if you want to invade other players as one of Rykard's own.

lockouts.name: Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy
lockouts.note: no further letters will appear

steps.text: Ride to the colosseum entrance at Stormhill, follow the red mark the letter put on your map, and touch the invasion sign to be sent after Old Knight Istvan.
Kill Istvan for his Scaled armour, then report back to Tanith; she pays with the Magma Shot sorcery and a second letter appears in the drawing room.

lockouts.name: Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy
lockouts.note: Tanith's reward is left lying where the letter was and the chain stops there

steps.text: Collect the second letter, then ride to the ravine below the Shaded Castle and use the invasion sign there to hunt Rileigh the Idle, a Roundtable confessor with a poisonous Scorpion's Stinger and a crossbow.
Report Rileigh's death to Tanith for the Serpentbone Blade, a poison katana, and the Red Letter appears in the drawing room.

lockouts.name: Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy
lockouts.note: the Serpentbone Blade hand-over is skipped

steps.text: Optional. If you have carried Rya's story far enough to meet her in her true serpent form and you then rest at a grace deep inside the manor, Tanith will hand you the Tonic of Forgetfulness for her.

lockouts.name: Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood
lockouts.note: Tanith's dialogue about Rya closes and the tonic can only be picked up from her chair after Rykard is dead

steps.text: Take the Red Letter, ride north-west of the Stargazers' Ruins to the Shack of the Lofty, and use the sign to invade Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood, the whip-wielding brother of Diallos.
Bring Juno's death back to Tanith. She pays with the Taker's Cameo talisman and, for the first time, offers to send you straight to her lord with the option "See the Lord".

lockouts.name: Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy
lockouts.note: the Taker's Cameo hand-over is skipped and the reward is left where the Red Letter was

steps.text: Take her up on it, but before you touch the fog, grab the Serpent-Hunter from the pile of corpses at the front of the arena; that great spear is built for this fight and can be picked up without waking anything.

Kill the God-Devouring Serpent to drop Rykard out of its mouth, then finish the second phase for his Great Rune and the Remembrance of the Blasphemous, which trades for the Blasphemous Blade or the Rykard's Rancor sorcery.
Go back to Tanith at the manor entrance and exhaust her; she thanks you for proving her lord was still weak and says she is leaving.
Fast travel to the grace inside Rykard's chamber to find her there instead, quietly eating what is left of him so that she can become his serpent.
Optional. If Patches gave you the Dancer's Castanets at the Shaded Castle, offer them to her here. She takes them and gives nothing back, so this is pure story.
Optional and final. Attacking Tanith kills her in one hit and summons Tanith's Knight to avenge her; beating the knight gives Aspects of the Crucible: Breath and the Consort's set she was wearing.
